above.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, paṭipucchāvinītā parisā nookkācitavinītā.
above.sujato: This is called an assembly educated in questioning, not in fancy talk.
above.english: This is called an assembly trained in cross-questioning and not in bombast.”

lines.pali: Imā kho, bhikkhave, dve parisā.
lines.sujato: These are the two assemblies.

lines.pali: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imāsaṁ dvinnaṁ parisānaṁ yadidaṁ paṭipucchāvinītā parisā nookkācitavinītā”ti.
lines.sujato: The better of these two assemblies is the assembly educated in questioning, not in fancy talk.”

above.pali: mayhameva sāvakānaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ, nāññesaṁ sāvakānaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalan’ti.
above.sujato: Only what is given to my disciples is very fruitful, not what is given to the disciples of others.’
above.english: Only what is given to my disciples bears great fruit, and not what is given to the disciples of others.”’

lines.pali: Ye te, bho gotama, evamāhaṁsu ‘samaṇo gotamo evamāha:
“mayhameva dānaṁ dātabbaṁ, nāññesaṁ dānaṁ dātabbaṁ.
Mayhameva sāvakānaṁ dānaṁ dātabbaṁ, nāññesaṁ sāvakānaṁ dānaṁ dātabbaṁ.
Mayhameva dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ, nāññesaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ.
Mayhameva sāvakānaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ, nāññesaṁ sāvakānaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalan”’ti.

below.pali: Kacci te bhoto gotamassa vuttavādino na ca bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ abhūtena abbhācikkhanti, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākaronti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānupāto gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgacchati?
below.sujato: I trust those who say this repeat what the worthy Gotama has said, and do not misrepresent him with an untruth? Is their explanation in line with the teaching? Are there any legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism?
below.english: Now those who report this: Are they reporting the Master Gotama’s actual words, are they not misrepresenting him with what is unfactual, are they answering in line with the Dhamma, so that no one whose thinking is in line with the Dhamma will have grounds for criticizing them?

above.pali: Yadapi, bhikkhave, adoso tadapi kusalamūlaṁ;
above.sujato: Love is a root of the skillful.
above.english: “Lack of aversion itself is skillful…

lines.pali: yadapi aduṭṭho abhisaṅkharoti kāyena vācāya manasā tadapi kusalaṁ;
lines.sujato: When a loving person chooses to act by way of body, speech, or mind, that too is skillful.

lines.pali: yadapi aduṭṭho dosena anabhibhūto apariyādinnacitto na parassa asatā dukkhaṁ uppādayati vadhena vā bandhanena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā pabbājanāya vā balavamhi balattho itipi tadapi kusalaṁ.
lines.sujato: When a loving person, not overcome by hate, doesn’t cause another to suffer under a false pretext—by execution or imprisonment or confiscation or condemnation or banishment—thinking ‘I’m powerful, I want power’, that too is skillful.

lines.pali: Itissame adosajā adosanidānā adosasamudayā adosapaccayā aneke kusalā dhammā sambhavanti.
lines.sujato: And so these many skillful things are produced in them, born, sourced, originated, and conditioned by love.

below.pali: Yadapi, bhikkhave, amoho tadapi kusalamūlaṁ;
below.sujato: Understanding is a root of the skillful.
below.english: “Lack of delusion itself is skillful.

above.pali: Idha, visākhe, ariyasāvako devatā anussarati:
above.sujato: It’s when a noble disciple recollects the deities:
above.english: There is the case where the disciple of the noble ones recollects the devas.…

lines.pali: ‘santi devā cātumahārājikā, santi devā tāvatiṁsā …pe… santi devā tatuttari.
lines.sujato: ‘There are the gods of the four great kings, the gods of the thirty-three, the gods of Yama, the joyful gods, the gods who love to imagine, the gods who control what is imagined by others, the gods of the Divinity’s host, and gods even higher than these.

lines.pali: Yathārūpāya saddhāya samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tatthupapannā, mayhampi tathārūpā saddhā saṁvijjati.
lines.sujato: When those deities passed away from here, they were reborn there because of their faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom. I, too, have the same kind of faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.’

lines.pali: Yathārūpena sīlena …
sutena …
cāgena …
paññāya samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tatthupapannā, mayhampi tathārūpā paññā saṁvijjatī’ti.

below.pali: Tassa attano ca tāsañca devatānaṁ saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarato cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti.
below.sujato: As they recollect the faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom of both themselves and those deities, their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up.
below.english: As he is recollecting the devas, his mind is cleansed, and joy arises; the defilements of his mind are abandoned.

above.pali: “Cattārome, bho gotama, puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
above.english: “Master Gotama, there are these four persons to be found existing in the world.…

lines.pali: Katame cattāro?
Idha, bho gotama, ekacco puggalo avaṇṇārahassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, no ca kho vaṇṇārahassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
Idha pana, bho gotama, ekacco puggalo vaṇṇārahassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, no ca kho avaṇṇārahassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
Idha pana, bho gotama, ekacco puggalo neva avaṇṇārahassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, no ca vaṇṇārahassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
Idha pana, bho gotama, ekacco puggalo avaṇṇārahassa ca avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, vaṇṇārahassa ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
Ime kho, bho gotama, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.

below.pali: Imesaṁ, bho gotama, catunnaṁ puggalānaṁ yvāyaṁ puggalo neva avaṇṇārahassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, no ca vaṇṇārahassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena;
below.sujato: “Worthy Gotama, of these four individuals, it is the individual who neither praises those deserving of praise at the right time, truthfully and correctly; nor criticizes those deserving of criticism at the right time, truthfully and correctly.
below.english: And of these four persons, Master Gotama, the one who neither speaks in dispraise of one deserving dispraise when it is accurate, factual, & timely, nor speaks in praise of one deserving praise when it is accurate, factual, & timely

above.pali: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
above.sujato: In the same way, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching …
above.english: In the same way, there is the case where a monk has mastered the Dhamma.…

lines.pali: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
Tassa te dhammā sotānugatā honti, vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.

below.sujato: But they die unmindful and are reborn in one of the orders of gods. …
below.english: Passing away when his mindfulness is muddled, he arises in a certain group of devas.…

above.pali: ‘yathā kho imassa āyasmato ummaggo yathā ca abhinīhāro yathā ca pañhāsamudāhāro, duppañño ayamāyasmā, nāyamāyasmā paññavā.
above.sujato: ‘Judging by this venerable’s approach, by what they’re getting at, and by how they discuss a question, they’re witless, not wise. …’
above.english: ‘From the way this person rises to an issue, from the way he applies (his reasoning), from the way he addresses a question…

lines.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
Tathā hi ayamāyasmā na ceva gambhīraṁ atthapadaṁ udāharati santaṁ paṇītaṁ atakkāvacaraṁ nipuṇaṁ paṇḍitavedanīyaṁ.
Yañca ayamāyasmā dhammaṁ bhāsati, tassa ca na paṭibalo saṅkhittena vā vitthārena vā atthaṁ ācikkhituṁ desetuṁ paññāpetuṁ paṭṭhapetuṁ vivarituṁ vibhajituṁ uttānīkātuṁ.

below.pali: Duppañño ayamāyasmā, nāyamāyasmā paññavā’ti.
below.english: he is dull, not discerning.’

above.pali: ‘yathā kho imassa āyasmato ummaggo yathā ca abhinīhāro yathā ca pañhāsamudāhāro, paññavā ayamāyasmā, nāyamāyasmā duppañño.
above.sujato: ‘Judging by this venerable’s approach, by what they’re getting at, and by how they articulate a question, they’re wise, not witless. …’
above.english: ‘From the way this person rises to an issue, from the way he applies (his reasoning), from the way he addresses a question… he is discerning, not dull.’

lines.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
Tathā hi ayamāyasmā gambhīrañceva atthapadaṁ udāharati santaṁ paṇītaṁ atakkāvacaraṁ nipuṇaṁ paṇḍitavedanīyaṁ.
Yañca ayamāyasmā dhammaṁ bhāsati, tassa ca paṭibalo saṅkhittena vā vitthārena vā atthaṁ ācikkhituṁ desetuṁ paññāpetuṁ paṭṭhapetuṁ vivarituṁ vibhajituṁ uttānīkātuṁ.
Paññavā ayamāyasmā, nāyamāyasmā duppañño’ti.

below.pali: ‘Sākacchāya, bhikkhave, paññā veditabbā, sā ca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṁ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññenā’ti, iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
below.sujato: That’s why I said that you can get to know a person’s wisdom by discussion. But only after a long time, not casually; only when attentive, not when inattentive; and only by the wise, not the witless.
below.english: “‘It’s through discussion that a person’s discernment may be known, and then only after a long period, not a short period; by one who is attentive, not by one who is inattentive; by one who is discerning, not by one who is not discerning’: Thus it was said. And in reference to this was it said.

above.pali: ye vacīsamārambhapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, vacīsamārambhā paṭiviratassa evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.
above.sujato: There are distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of instigating verbal activity. These don’t occur in someone who refrains from such verbal activity.
above.english: “Vappa, as for any effluents causing trouble & vexation that arise in dependence on verbal activity…

lines.pali: So navañca kammaṁ na karoti, purāṇañca kammaṁ phussa phussa byantīkaroti.
lines.sujato: They don’t perform any new deeds, and old deeds are eliminated by experiencing their results little by little.

lines.pali: Sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṁ veditabbā viññūhi.
lines.sujato: This wearing away is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

lines.pali: Passasi no tvaṁ, vappa, taṁ ṭhānaṁ yatonidānaṁ purisaṁ dukkhavedaniyā āsavā assaveyyuṁ abhisamparāyan”ti?
lines.sujato: Do you see any reason why defilements giving rise to painful feelings would defile that person in the next life?”

below.pali: ye manosamārambhapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, manosamārambhā paṭiviratassa evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.
below.sujato: There are distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of instigating mental activity. These don’t occur in someone who refrains from such mental activity.
below.english: any effluents causing trouble & vexation that arise in dependence on mental activity…

below.pali: ye avijjāpaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, avijjāvirāgā vijjuppādā evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.
below.sujato: There are distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of ignorance. These don’t occur when ignorance fades away and knowledge arises.
below.english: any effluents causing trouble & vexation that arise in dependence on ignorance: From the fading of ignorance, and from the arising of clear knowing, those effluents causing trouble & vexation do not exist for him.

above.pali: Atha kho so bhikkhu taṁ saddhivihārikaṁ bhikkhuṁ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
above.sujato: Then that mendicant took his protégé to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,
above.english: So that monk [the preceptor], taking his student along, went to the Blessed One. On arrival, having bowed down to the Blessed One, he sat to one side. As he was sitting there he [told the Blessed One what his student had said.]

lines.pali: “ayaṁ, bhante, bhikkhu evamāha:
lines.sujato: “Sir, this mendicant says this:

lines.pali: ‘etarahi me, bhante, madhurakajāto ceva kāyo, disā ca maṁ na pakkhāyanti, dhammā ca me nappaṭibhanti, thinamiddhañca me cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, anabhirato ca brahmacariyaṁ carāmi, atthi ca me dhammesu vicikicchā’”ti.
lines.sujato: ‘Now, sir, my body feels like it’s drugged. I’m disorientated, the teachings don’t spring to mind, and dullness and drowsiness fill my mind. I lead the spiritual life dissatisfied, and have doubts about the teachings.’”

below.pali: “Evañhetaṁ, bhikkhu, hoti indriyesu aguttadvārassa, bhojane amattaññuno, jāgariyaṁ ananuyuttassa, avipassakassa kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ, pubbarattāpararattaṁ bodhipakkhiyānaṁ dhammānaṁ bhāvanānuyogaṁ ananuyuttassa viharato, yaṁ madhurakajāto ceva kāyo hoti, disā cassa na pakkhāyanti, dhammā ca taṁ nappaṭibhanti, thinamiddhañcassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, anabhirato ca brahmacariyaṁ carati, hoti cassa dhammesu vicikicchā.
below.sujato: “That’s how it is, mendicant, when your sense doors are unguarded, you eat too much, you’re not dedicated to wakefulness, you’re unable to discern skillful qualities, and you don’t pursue the development of the qualities on the side of awakening in the evening and toward dawn. Your body feels like it’s drugged. You’re disorientated, the teachings don’t spring to mind, and dullness and drowsiness fill your mind. You lead the spiritual life dissatisfied, and have doubts about the teachings.
below.english: [The Blessed One said:] “That’s how it is, monk, for one who lives with his senses unguarded, knowing no moderation in food, not committed to wakefulness, with no insight into skillful qualities, and not committed to the development of the wings to awakening in the early & late hours of the night. It’s as if his body is drugged. He’s lost his bearings. Things aren’t clear to him. His mind keeps being overwhelmed with sloth & torpor. He leads the holy life dissatisfied. He has uncertainty about the teachings.

above.pali: Atha kho so bhikkhu taṁ saddhivihārikaṁ bhikkhuṁ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
above.sujato: Then that mendicant took his protégé to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,
above.english: So that monk [the preceptor], taking his student along, went to the Blessed One. On arrival, having bowed down to the Blessed One, he sat to one side. As he was sitting there he [told the Blessed One what his student had said.]

lines.pali: “ayaṁ, bhante, bhikkhu evamāha:
lines.sujato: “Sir, this mendicant says this:

lines.pali: ‘etarahi me, bhante, na ceva madhurakajāto kāyo, disā ca me pakkhāyanti, dhammā ca maṁ paṭibhanti, thinamiddhañca me cittaṁ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, abhirato ca brahmacariyaṁ carāmi, natthi ca me dhammesu vicikicchā’”ti.
lines.sujato: ‘Now, sir, my body doesn’t feel like it’s drugged. I’m not disorientated, the teachings spring to mind, and dullness and drowsiness don’t fill my mind. I lead the spiritual life satisfied, and have no doubts about the teachings.’”

below.pali: “Evañhetaṁ, bhikkhu, hoti indriyesu guttadvārassa, bhojane mattaññuno, jāgariyaṁ anuyuttassa, vipassakassa kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ, pubbarattāpararattaṁ bodhipakkhiyānaṁ dhammānaṁ bhāvanānuyogaṁ anuyuttassa viharato, yaṁ na ceva madhurakajāto kāyo hoti, disā cassa pakkhāyanti, dhammā ca taṁ paṭibhanti, thinamiddhañcassa cittaṁ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, abhirato ca brahmacariyaṁ carati, na cassa hoti dhammesu vicikicchā.
below.sujato: “That’s how it is, mendicant, when your sense doors are guarded, you’re moderate in eating, you’re dedicated to wakefulness, you’re able to discern skillful qualities, and you pursue the development of the qualities on the side of awakening in the evening and toward dawn. Your body doesn’t feel like it’s drugged. You’re not disorientated, the teachings spring to mind, and dullness and drowsiness don’t fill your mind. You lead the spiritual life satisfied, and have no doubts about the teachings.
below.english: [The Blessed One said:] “That’s how it is, monk, for one who lives with his senses guarded, knowing moderation in food, committed to wakefulness, with insight into skillful qualities, and committed to the development of the wings to awakening in the early & late hours of the night. His body is no longer drugged and he’s regained his bearings. Things are clear to him. His mind is no longer overwhelmed with sloth & torpor. He leads the holy life satisfied. He has no uncertainty about the teachings.

above.pali: Tassa taṁ ṭhānaṁ abhiṇhaṁ paccavekkhato sabbaso vā duccaritaṁ pahīyati tanu vā pana hoti.
above.sujato: Reviewing this subject often, they entirely give up bad conduct, or at least reduce it.
above.english: But when they often reflect on that fact, that bad conduct in body, speech, & mind will either be entirely abandoned or grow weaker.…

lines.pali: Idaṁ kho, bhikkhave, atthavasaṁ paṭicca ‘kammassakomhi, kammadāyādo kammayoni kammabandhu kammapaṭisaraṇo, yaṁ kammaṁ karissāmi—
lines.sujato: This is the advantage for a woman or a man, a layperson or a renunciate of often reviewing like this: ‘I am the owner of my deeds and heir to my deeds. Deeds are my womb, my relative, and my refuge.

lines.pali: kalyāṇaṁ vā pāpakaṁ vā—
lines.sujato: I shall be the heir of whatever deeds I do, whether good or bad.’

lines.pali: tassa dāyādo bhavissāmī’ti abhiṇhaṁ paccavekkhitabbaṁ itthiyā vā purisena vā gahaṭṭhena vā pabbajitena vā.

below.pali: Sa kho so, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
below.sujato: Then that noble disciple reflects:
below.english: “Now, a disciple of the noble ones considers this:

above.pali: ‘Na kho ahaññeveko byādhidhammo byādhiṁ anatīto, atha kho yāvatā sattānaṁ āgati gati cuti upapatti sabbe sattā byādhidhammā byādhiṁ anatītā’ti.
above.sujato: ‘It’s not just me who is liable to get sick, not being exempt from sickness. For all sentient beings get sick according to their nature, as long as they come and go, pass away and are reborn.’
above.english: “Further, a disciple of the noble ones considers this: ‘I am not the only one subject to illness, who has not gone beyond illness’.…

lines.pali: Tassa taṁ ṭhānaṁ abhiṇhaṁ paccavekkhato maggo sañjāyati.
lines.sujato: When they review this subject often, the path is born in them.

lines.pali: So taṁ maggaṁ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti.
lines.sujato: They cultivate, develop, and make much of it.

lines.pali: Tassa taṁ maggaṁ āsevato bhāvayato bahulīkaroto saṁyojanāni sabbaso pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti.
lines.sujato: By doing so, they give up the fetters and eliminate the underlying tendencies.

below.pali: ‘Na kho ahaññeveko maraṇadhammo maraṇaṁ anatīto, atha kho yāvatā sattānaṁ āgati gati cuti upapatti sabbe sattā maraṇadhammā maraṇaṁ anatītā’ti.
below.sujato: ‘It’s not just me who is liable to die, not being exempt from death. For all sentient beings die according to their nature, as long as they come and go, pass away and are reborn.’
below.english: ‘I am not the only one subject to death, who has not gone beyond death’.…

above.pali: ‘Na kho ahaññeveko maraṇadhammo maraṇaṁ anatīto, atha kho yāvatā sattānaṁ āgati gati cuti upapatti sabbe sattā maraṇadhammā maraṇaṁ anatītā’ti.
above.sujato: ‘It’s not just me who is liable to die, not being exempt from death. For all sentient beings die according to their nature, as long as they come and go, pass away and are reborn.’
above.english: ‘I am not the only one subject to death, who has not gone beyond death’.…

lines.pali: Tassa taṁ ṭhānaṁ abhiṇhaṁ paccavekkhato maggo sañjāyati.
lines.sujato: When they review this subject often, the path is born in them.

lines.pali: So taṁ maggaṁ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti.
lines.sujato: They cultivate, develop, and make much of it.

lines.pali: Tassa taṁ maggaṁ āsevato bhāvayato bahulīkaroto saṁyojanāni sabbaso pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti.
lines.sujato: By doing so, they give up the fetters and eliminate the underlying tendencies.

below.pali: ‘Na kho mayhevekassa sabbehi piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo, atha kho yāvatā sattānaṁ āgati gati cuti upapatti sabbesaṁ sattānaṁ piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo’ti.
below.sujato: ‘It’s not just me who must be parted and separated from all I hold dear and beloved. For all sentient beings must be parted and separated from all they hold dear and beloved, as long as they come and go, pass away and are reborn.’
below.english: ‘I am not the only one who will grow different, separate from all that is dear & appealing to me’.…

above.pali: ‘Na kho mayhevekassa sabbehi piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo, atha kho yāvatā sattānaṁ āgati gati cuti upapatti sabbesaṁ sattānaṁ piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo’ti.
above.sujato: ‘It’s not just me who must be parted and separated from all I hold dear and beloved. For all sentient beings must be parted and separated from all they hold dear and beloved, as long as they come and go, pass away and are reborn.’
above.english: ‘I am not the only one who will grow different, separate from all that is dear & appealing to me’.…

lines.pali: Tassa taṁ ṭhānaṁ abhiṇhaṁ paccavekkhato maggo sañjāyati.
lines.sujato: When they review this subject often, the path is born in them.

lines.pali: So taṁ maggaṁ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti.
lines.sujato: They cultivate, develop, and make much of it.

lines.pali: Tassa taṁ maggaṁ āsevato bhāvayato bahulīkaroto saṁyojanāni sabbaso pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti.
lines.sujato: By doing so, they give up the fetters and eliminate the underlying tendencies.

below.pali: ‘Na kho ahaññeveko kammassako kammadāyādo kammayoni kammabandhu kammapaṭisaraṇo, yaṁ kammaṁ karissāmi—kalyāṇaṁ vā pāpakaṁ vā—tassa dāyādo bhavissāmi;
below.sujato: ‘It’s not just me who shall be the owner of my deeds and heir to my deeds.
below.english: “A disciple of the noble ones considers this: ‘I am not the only one who is the owner of actions, heir to actions, born of actions, related through actions, and have actions as my arbitrator; who—whatever I do, for good or for evil, to that will I fall heir.

above.pali: Dutiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ āmantesi:
above.sujato: And a second time …
above.english: A second time…

lines.pali: “kati nu kho, udāyi, anussatiṭṭhānānī”ti?
Dutiyampi kho āyasmā udāyī tuṇhī ahosi.

below.pali: Tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ āmantesi:
below.sujato: and a third time, the Buddha said to him,
below.english: A third time, the Blessed One addressed Ven. Udāyin,

above.pali: Seyyathāpi vā pana passeyya sarīraṁ sīvathikāya chaṭṭitaṁ kākehi vā khajjamānaṁ kulalehi vā khajjamānaṁ gijjhehi vā khajjamānaṁ sunakhehi vā khajjamānaṁ siṅgālehi vā khajjamānaṁ vividhehi vā pāṇakajātehi khajjamānaṁ.
above.sujato: Or suppose they were to see a corpse thrown in a charnel ground being devoured by crows, hawks, vultures, hounds, jackals, and many kinds of little creatures.
above.english: “Or, as if he were to see a corpse cast away in a charnel ground, being chewed by crows, being chewed by vultures, being chewed by hawks, being chewed by dogs, being chewed by hyenas, being chewed by various other creatures…

lines.pali: So imameva kāyaṁ evaṁ upasaṁharati:
lines.sujato: They’d compare it with their own body:

lines.pali: ‘ayampi kho kāyo evaṁdhammo evaṁbhāvī evaṁanatīto’ti.
lines.sujato: ‘This body is also of that same nature, that same kind, and cannot go beyond that.’

below.pali: Seyyathāpi vā pana passeyya sarīraṁ sīvathikāya chaṭṭitaṁ aṭṭhikasaṅkhalikaṁ samaṁsalohitaṁ nhārusambandhaṁ …pe…
below.sujato: Furthermore, suppose they were to see a corpse thrown in a charnel ground, a skeleton with flesh and blood, held together by sinews …
below.english: a skeleton smeared with flesh & blood, connected with tendons…

above.pali: ‘lābhasakkārasilokaṁ nūna ayamāyasmā nikāmayamāno pavivekādhimutto’ti.
above.sujato: ‘Maybe this venerable is dedicated to seclusion because they enjoy possessions, honor, and popularity.’
above.english: ‘Perhaps it is because he desires gain, honor, & fame that this venerable one is dedicated to seclusion’…

lines.pali: Na kho panetaṁ, bhante, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
lines.sujato: But it should not be seen like this. …

lines.pali: Khīṇāsavo, bhante, bhikkhu vusitavā katakaraṇīyo karaṇīyaṁ attano asamanupassanto katassa vā paṭicayaṁ khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā pavivekādhimutto hoti, khayā dosassa vītadosattā pavivekādhimutto hoti, khayā mohassa vītamohattā pavivekādhimutto hoti.

below.pali: ‘sīlabbataparāmāsaṁ nūna ayamāyasmā sārato paccāgacchanto abyāpajjādhimutto’ti.
below.sujato: ‘Maybe this venerable is dedicated to kindness because they believe that adhering to precepts and observances is essential.’
below.english: ‘Perhaps it is because he falls back on attachment to habits & practices as being essential that he is dedicated to non-afflictiveness,’

above.pali: Kāmarāgānusayassa pahānāya samucchedāya brahmacariyaṁ vussati, paṭighānusayassa …pe…
above.sujato: The underlying tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, views, doubt, conceit, desire to be reborn, and ignorance.
above.english: The obsession of sensual passion, the obsession of resistance, the obsession of views, the obsession of uncertainty, the obsession of conceit, the obsession of passion for becoming, the obsession of ignorance.

lines.pali: diṭṭhānusayassa …
vicikicchānusayassa …
mānānusayassa …
bhavarāgānusayassa …
avijjānusayassa pahānāya samucchedāya brahmacariyaṁ vussati.

below.pali: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, sattannaṁ anusayānaṁ pahānāya samucchedāya brahmacariyaṁ vussati.
below.sujato: The spiritual life is lived to give up and cut out these seven underlying tendencies.
below.english: With the abandoning & destruction of these seven obsessions, the holy life is fulfilled.

above.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjati sādhu saddhā kusalesu dhammesu, sādhu hirī …pe…
above.sujato: It’s the kind of individual who, rising up, thinks: ‘It’s good to have faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities.’
above.english: There is the case where an individual comes to the surface, (seeing,) ‘Conviction in skillful qualities is good, a sense of shame is good, a sense of compunction (over the results of actions) is good, persistence is good, discernment with regard to skillful qualities is good.’

lines.pali: sādhu ottappaṁ …
sādhu vīriyaṁ …
sādhu paññā kusalesu dhammesūti.

below.pali: Tassa sā saddhā neva tiṭṭhati no vaḍḍhati hāyatiyeva, tassa sā hirī …pe…
below.sujato: However their faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom don’t last or grow, but dwindle away.
below.english: But his conviction neither remains nor grows, but simply wanes away. His sense of shame, his sense of compunction, his persistence, his discernment neither remain nor grow, but simply wane away.

above.pali: Tassa sā saddhā neva tiṭṭhati no vaḍḍhati hāyatiyeva, tassa sā hirī …pe…
above.sujato: However their faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom don’t last or grow, but dwindle away.
above.english: But his conviction neither remains nor grows, but simply wanes away. His sense of shame, his sense of compunction, his persistence, his discernment neither remain nor grow, but simply wane away.

lines.pali: tassa taṁ ottappaṁ …
tassa taṁ vīriyaṁ …
tassa sā paññā neva tiṭṭhati no vaḍḍhati hāyatiyeva.

below.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo ummujjitvā nimujjati.
below.sujato: This kind of individual rises up then sinks under.
below.english: That’s how an individual, on coming to the surface, sinks down again.

above.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjati sādhu saddhā kusalesu dhammesu, sādhu hirī …pe…
above.sujato: It’s the kind of individual who, rising up, thinks: ‘It’s good to have faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities.’
above.english: There is the case where an individual comes to the surface, (seeing,) ‘Conviction in skillful qualities is good, a sense of shame is good, a sense of compunction is good, persistence is good, discernment with regard to skillful qualities is good.’

lines.pali: sādhu ottappaṁ …
sādhu vīriyaṁ …
sādhu paññā kusalesu dhammesūti.

below.pali: Tassa sā saddhā neva hāyati no vaḍḍhati ṭhitā hoti.
below.sujato: And their faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom lasts, neither dwindling nor growing.
below.english: His conviction doesn’t wane, but instead develops & remains.

above.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjati sādhu saddhā kusalesu dhammesu, sādhu hirī …pe…
above.sujato: It’s the kind of individual who, rising up, thinks: ‘It’s good to have faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities.’
above.english: There is the case where an individual comes to the surface, (seeing,) ‘Conviction in skillful qualities is good, a sense of shame is good, a sense of compunction is good, persistence is good, discernment with regard to skillful qualities is good.’

lines.pali: sādhu ottappaṁ …
sādhu vīriyaṁ …
sādhu paññā kusalesu dhammesūti.

below.pali: So tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.
below.sujato: With the ending of three fetters they’re a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.
below.english: With the total ending of (the first) three fetters, he becomes a stream-winner, steadfast, never again destined for states of woe, headed for self-awakening.

above.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjati sādhu saddhā kusalesu dhammesu, sādhu hirī …pe…
above.sujato: It’s the kind of individual who, rising up, thinks: ‘It’s good to have faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities.’
above.english: There is the case where an individual comes to the surface, (seeing,) ‘Conviction in skillful qualities is good, a sense of shame is good, a sense of compunction is good, persistence is good, discernment with regard to skillful qualities is good.’

lines.pali: sādhu ottappaṁ …
sādhu vīriyaṁ …
sādhu paññā kusalesu dhammesūti.

below.pali: So tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṁ tanuttā sakadāgāmī hoti, sakideva imaṁ lokaṁ āgantvā dukkhassantaṁ karoti.
below.sujato: With the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, they’re a once-returner. They come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.
below.english: With the total ending of (the first) three fetters, and with the attenuation of passion, aversion, & delusion, he becomes a once-returner, who—on returning only one more time to this world—will make an ending to stress.

above.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjati sādhu saddhā kusalesu dhammesu, sādhu hirī …pe…
above.sujato: It’s the kind of individual who, rising up, thinks: ‘It’s good to have faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities.’
above.english: There is the case where an individual comes to the surface, (seeing,) ‘Conviction in skillful qualities is good, a sense of shame is good, a sense of compunction is good, persistence is good, discernment with regard to skillful qualities is good.’

lines.pali: sādhu ottappaṁ …
sādhu vīriyaṁ …
sādhu paññā kusalesu dhammesūti.

below.pali: So pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.
below.sujato: With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re reborn spontaneously. They are extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.
below.english: With the total ending of the five lower fetters, he is due to arise spontaneously (in the Pure Abodes), there to be totally unbound, never again to return from that world.

above.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjati sādhu saddhā kusalesu dhammesu, sādhu hirī …pe…
above.sujato: It’s the kind of individual who, rising up, thinks: ‘It’s good to have faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities.’
above.english: There is the case where an individual comes to the surface, (seeing,) ‘Conviction in skillful qualities is good, a sense of shame is good, a sense of compunction is good, persistence is good, discernment with regard to skillful qualities is good.’

lines.pali: sādhu ottappaṁ …
sādhu vīriyaṁ …
sādhu paññā kusalesu dhammesūti.

below.pali: So āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
below.sujato: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.
below.english: With the ending of effluents, he enters & remains in the effluent-free awareness-release & discernment-release, having directly known and realized them for himself right in the here & now.

above.pali: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, sīha, kaṁ nu kho arahanto paṭhamaṁ upasaṅkamantā upasaṅkameyyuṁ:
above.sujato: “Which do you think the perfected ones will first approach?”
above.english: “What do you think, Sīha? Whom would arahants, when visiting, first visit…?”

lines.pali: ‘yo vā so puriso assaddho maccharī kadariyo paribhāsako, yo vā so puriso saddho dānapati anuppadānarato’”ti?
“Yo so, bhante, puriso assaddho maccharī kadariyo paribhāsako, kintaṁ arahanto paṭhamaṁ upasaṅkamantā upasaṅkamissanti.

below.pali: Yo ca kho so, bhante, puriso saddho dānapati anuppadānarato taṁyeva arahanto paṭhamaṁ upasaṅkamantā upasaṅkameyyuṁ”.
below.sujato: “They’d first approach the faithful donor who loves charity.”
below.english: “…The man of conviction, a master of giving, one who delights in providing support…”

above.pali: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, sīha, kassa nu kho arahanto paṭhamaṁ paṭiggaṇhantā paṭiggaṇheyyuṁ:
above.sujato: “Which do you think the perfected ones will receive alms from first?”
above.english: “What do you think, Sīha? From whom would arahants, when receiving (gifts), first receive (gifts)…?”

lines.pali: ‘yo vā so puriso assaddho maccharī kadariyo paribhāsako, yo vā so puriso saddho dānapati anuppadānarato’”ti?
“Yo so, bhante, puriso assaddho maccharī kadariyo paribhāsako, kintaṁ tassa arahanto paṭhamaṁ paṭiggaṇhantā paṭiggaṇhissanti.

below.pali: Yo ca kho so, bhante, puriso saddho dānapati anuppadānarato tasseva arahanto paṭhamaṁ paṭiggaṇhantā paṭiggaṇheyyuṁ”.
below.sujato: “They’d receive alms first from the faithful donor who loves charity.”

above.pali: Tassa ce, āvuso, bhikkhuno iminā vihārena viharato vitakkasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti, svassa hoti ābādho.
above.sujato: While a mendicant is practicing such a meditation, if perception and focus accompanied by placing of the mind beset them, that’s an affliction for them.
above.english: If, as he remains there, he is beset with attention to perceptions dealing with directed thought, that is an affliction for him.…

lines.pali: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, sukhino dukkhaṁ uppajjeyya yāvadeva ābādhāya;
lines.sujato: Suppose a happy person were to experience pain; that would be an affliction for them.

lines.pali: evamevassa te vitakkasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti. Svassa hoti ābādho.
lines.sujato: In the same way, should perception and focus accompanied by placing of the mind beset them, that’s an affliction for them.

lines.pali: Yo kho panāvuso, ābādho dukkhametaṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā.
lines.sujato: And affliction has been called suffering by the Buddha.

lines.pali: Imināpi kho etaṁ, āvuso, pariyāyena veditabbaṁ yathā sukhaṁ nibbānaṁ.
lines.sujato: That too is a way to understand how extinguishment is bliss.

above.pali: ‘etaṁ santaṁ etaṁ paṇītaṁ yadidaṁ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānan’ti.

above.english: ‘This is peace, this is exquisite—the pacification of all fabrications; the relinquishing of all acquisitions; the ending of craving; dispassion; cessation; unbinding.’

lines.pali: So tattha ṭhito āsavānaṁ khayaṁ pāpuṇāti.
lines.sujato: Abiding in that they attain the ending of defilements.

lines.pali: No ce āsavānaṁ khayaṁ pāpuṇāti, teneva dhammarāgena tāya dhammanandiyā pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.
lines.sujato: If they don’t attain the ending of defilements, with the ending of the five lower fetters they’re reborn spontaneously, because of their passion and love for that meditation. They are extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.

below.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, issāso vā issāsantevāsī vā tiṇapurisarūpake vā mattikāpuñje vā yoggaṁ karitvā, so aparena samayena dūrepātī ca hoti akkhaṇavedhī ca mahato ca kāyassa padāletā;

below.english: “Suppose that an archer or archer’s apprentice were to practice on a straw man or mound of clay, so that after a while he would become able to shoot long distances, to fire accurate shots in rapid succession, and to pierce great masses.

above.pali: ‘catutthampāhaṁ, bhikkhave, jhānaṁ nissāya āsavānaṁ khayaṁ vadāmī’ti, iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ.
above.sujato: ‘The fourth absorption is also a basis for ending the defilements.’ …
above.english: and fourth jhāna.]

lines.pali: Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṁ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṁ catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
So yadeva tattha hoti rūpagataṁ vedanāgataṁ saññāgataṁ saṅkhāragataṁ viññāṇagataṁ, te dhamme aniccato dukkhato rogato gaṇḍato sallato aghato ābādhato parato palokato suññato anattato samanupassati.
So tehi dhammehi cittaṁ paṭivāpeti.
So tehi dhammehi cittaṁ paṭivāpetvā amatāya dhātuyā cittaṁ upasaṁharati:
‘etaṁ santaṁ etaṁ paṇītaṁ yadidaṁ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānan’ti.
So tattha ṭhito āsavānaṁ khayaṁ pāpuṇāti.
No ce āsavānaṁ khayaṁ pāpuṇāti, teneva dhammarāgena tāya dhammanandiyā pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.

below.pali: ‘Ākāsānañcāyatanampāhaṁ, bhikkhave, jhānaṁ nissāya āsavānaṁ khayaṁ vadāmī’ti, iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ.
below.sujato: ‘The dimension of infinite space is also a basis for ending the defilements.’
below.english: “‘I tell you, the ending of the effluents depends on the dimension of the infinitude of space.’

above.pali: ‘etaṁ santaṁ etaṁ paṇītaṁ yadidaṁ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānan’ti.
above.sujato: ‘This is peaceful; this is sublime—that is, the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.’
above.english: ‘This is peace, this is exquisite—the pacification of all fabrications; the relinquishing of all acquisitions; the ending of craving; dispassion; cessation; unbinding.’

lines.pali: So tattha ṭhito āsavānaṁ khayaṁ pāpuṇāti.
lines.sujato: Abiding in that they attain the ending of defilements.

lines.pali: No ce āsavānaṁ khayaṁ pāpuṇāti, teneva dhammarāgena tāya dhammanandiyā pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.
lines.sujato: If they don’t attain the ending of defilements, with the ending of the five lower fetters they’re reborn spontaneously, because of their passion and love for that meditation. They are extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.

below.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, issāso vā issāsantevāsī vā tiṇapurisarūpake vā mattikāpuñje vā yoggaṁ karitvā, so aparena samayena dūrepātī ca hoti akkhaṇavedhī ca mahato ca kāyassa padāletā;
below.sujato: It’s like an archer or their apprentice who first practices on a straw man or a clay model. At a later time they become a long-distance shooter, a marksman, who shatters large objects.
below.english: “Suppose that an archer or archer's apprentice were to practice on a straw man or mound of clay, so that after a while he would become able to shoot long distances, to fire accurate shots in rapid succession, and to pierce great masses.

above.pali: atha uttarāya disāya …
above.sujato: Then the man standing in the north …
above.english: & northern directions.]

lines.pali: atha dakkhiṇāya disāya ṭhito puriso evaṁ vadeyya:
lines.sujato: Then the man standing in the south would say:

lines.pali: ‘ahaṁ gamanena lokassa antaṁ pāpuṇissāmī’ti.
lines.sujato: ‘I will reach the end of the world by traveling.’

lines.pali: So aññatreva asitapītakhāyitasāyitā aññatra uccārapassāvakammā aññatra niddākilamathapaṭivinodanā vassasatāyuko vassasatajīvī vassasataṁ gantvā appatvāva lokassa antaṁ antarā kālaṁ kareyya.
lines.sujato: Though he’d travel for his whole lifespan of a hundred years—pausing only to eat and drink, go to the toilet, and sleep to dispel weariness—he’d die along the way, never reaching the end of the world.

below.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
below.sujato: Why is that?

lines.sujato: This is called a mendicant who, having gone to the end of the world, meditates at the end of the world.

lines.sujato: Others say of them:

lines.pali: ‘ayampi lokapariyāpanno, ayampi anissaṭo lokamhā’ti.
lines.sujato: ‘They’re included in the world, and haven’t yet left the world.’

lines.sujato: And I also say this:

lines.pali: ‘ayampi lokapariyāpanno, ayampi anissaṭo lokamhā’ti.
lines.sujato: ‘They’re included in the world, and haven’t yet left the world.’

below.sujato: Furthermore, take a mendicant who, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, enters and remains in the cessation of perception and feeling. And, having seen with wisdom, their defilements come to an end.
below.english: “And further, with the complete transcending of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, he enters & remains in the cessation of perception & feeling. And as he sees (that) with discernment, effluents are completely ended.

lines.pali: tasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye bhikkhussa evaṁ hoti:
lines.sujato: At that time the mendicant thinks,

lines.pali: ‘bhīruttānagatena kho dānāhaṁ etarahi attanā viharāmi akaraṇīyo mārassā’ti.
lines.sujato: ‘Now I’m in a secure location and Māra can’t do anything to me.’

lines.pali: Mārassāpi, bhikkhave, pāpimato evaṁ hoti:
lines.sujato: And Māra the Wicked also thinks,

lines.pali: ‘bhīruttānagatena kho dāni bhikkhu etarahi attanā viharati, akaraṇīyo mayhan’ti.
lines.sujato: ‘Now the mendicant is in a secure location and we can’t do anything to them.’

below.pali: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
below.sujato: There’s a time when a mendicant, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.
below.english: “On whatever occasion a monk, with the complete transcending of perceptions of (physical) form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and not attending to perceptions of multiplicity, (perceiving,) ‘Infinite space,’ enters the dimension of the infinitude of space:

above.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, nippītike cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato.
above.sujato: But my mind did not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in freedom from rapture. I didn’t see it as peaceful.
above.english: But my heart didn’t leap up at being without rapture, didn’t grow confident, steadfast, or released, (though) seeing it as peace.…

lines.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
lines.sujato: Then I thought,

lines.pali: ‘ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo, yena me nippītike cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato’?
lines.sujato: ‘What is the cause, what is the reason why my mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in freedom from rapture? Why don’t I see it as peaceful?’

lines.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
lines.sujato: Then I thought,

lines.pali: ‘pītiyā kho me ādīnavo adiṭṭho, so ca me abahulīkato, nippītike ca ānisaṁso anadhigato, so ca me anāsevito.
lines.sujato: ‘I haven’t seen the drawbacks of rapture, and so I haven’t cultivated that. I haven’t realized the benefits of freedom from rapture, and so I haven’t developed that.

lines.pali: Tasmā me nippītike cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato’.
lines.sujato: That’s why my mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in freedom from rapture. And it’s why I don’t see it as peaceful.’

lines.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
lines.sujato: Then I thought,

lines.pali: ‘sace kho ahaṁ pītiyā ādīnavaṁ disvā taṁ bahulaṁ kareyyaṁ, nippītike ānisaṁsaṁ adhigamma tamāseveyyaṁ, ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ vijjati yaṁ me nippītike cittaṁ pakkhandeyya pasīdeyya santiṭṭheyya vimucceyya etaṁ santanti passato’.
lines.sujato: ‘Suppose that, seeing the drawbacks of rapture, I were to cultivate that. And suppose that, realizing the benefits of freedom from rapture, I were to develop that. It’s possible that my mind would leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in being free from rapture. And I would see it as peaceful.’

below.pali: So kho ahaṁ, ānanda, aparena samayena pītiyā ādīnavaṁ disvā taṁ bahulamakāsiṁ, nippītike ānisaṁsaṁ adhigamma tamāseviṁ.
below.sujato: And so, after some time, I saw the drawbacks of rapture and cultivated that, and I realized the benefits of freedom from rapture and developed that.
below.english: So at a later time, having seen the drawback of rapture, I pursued that theme; having understood the reward of being without rapture, I familiarized myself with it.

lines.pali: ‘sace kho ahaṁ viññāṇañcāyatane ādīnavaṁ disvā taṁ bahulaṁ kareyyaṁ, ākiñcaññāyatane ānisaṁsaṁ adhigamma tamāseveyyaṁ, ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ vijjati yaṁ me ākiñcaññāyatane cittaṁ pakkhandeyya pasīdeyya santiṭṭheyya vimucceyya etaṁ santanti passato’.
lines.sujato: ‘Suppose that, seeing the drawbacks of the dimension of infinite consciousness, I were to cultivate that. And suppose that, realizing the benefits of the dimension of nothingness, I were to develop that. It’s possible that my mind would leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in the dimension of nothingness. And I would see it as peaceful.’

below.pali: So kho ahaṁ, ānanda, aparena samayena viññāṇañcāyatane ādīnavaṁ disvā taṁ bahulamakāsiṁ, ākiñcaññāyatane ānisaṁsaṁ adhigamma tamāseviṁ.
below.sujato: And so, after some time, I saw the drawbacks of the dimension of infinite consciousness and cultivated that, and I realized the benefits of the dimension of nothingness and developed that.
below.english: So at a later time, having seen the drawback of the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness, I pursued that theme; having understood the reward of the dimension of nothingness, I familiarized myself with it.

above.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato.
above.sujato: But my mind did not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. I didn’t see it as peaceful.
above.english: But my heart didn’t leap up at the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, didn’t grow confident, steadfast, or released, (though) seeing it as peace.…

lines.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
lines.sujato: Then I thought,

lines.pali: ‘ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo, yena me nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato’?
lines.sujato: ‘What is the cause, what is the reason why my mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception? Why don’t I see it as peaceful?’

lines.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
lines.sujato: Then I thought,

lines.pali: ‘ākiñcaññāyatane kho me ādīnavo adiṭṭho, so ca me abahulīkato, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane ca ānisaṁso anadhigato, so ca me anāsevito.
lines.sujato: ‘I haven’t seen the drawbacks of the dimension of nothingness, and so I haven’t cultivated that. I haven’t realized the benefits of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, and so I haven’t developed that.

lines.pali: Tasmā me nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati etaṁ santanti passato’.
lines.sujato: That’s why my mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. And it’s why I don’t see it as peaceful.’

lines.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, ānanda, etadahosi:
lines.sujato: Then I thought,

below.pali: So kho ahaṁ, ānanda, aparena samayena ākiñcaññāyatane ādīnavaṁ disvā taṁ bahulamakāsiṁ, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane ānisaṁsaṁ adhigamma tamāseviṁ.

above.sujato: “When asked about all these points, you say that’s not your view.

lines.sujato: Then they reflect:

lines.pali: ‘idampi kho catutthaṁ jhānaṁ abhisaṅkhataṁ abhisañcetayitaṁ’.
lines.sujato: ‘Even this fourth absorption is produced by choices and intentions.’

lines.pali: ‘Yaṁ kho pana kiñci abhisaṅkhataṁ abhisañcetayitaṁ tadaniccaṁ nirodhadhamman’ti pajānāti.
lines.sujato: They understand: ‘But whatever is produced by choices and intentions is impermanent and liable to cessation.’

lines.pali: So tattha ṭhito āsavānaṁ khayaṁ pāpuṇāti;
lines.sujato: Abiding in that they attain the ending of defilements.

lines.pali: no ce āsavānaṁ khayaṁ pāpuṇāti, teneva dhammarāgena tāya dhammanandiyā pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.
lines.sujato: If they don’t attain the ending of defilements, with the ending of the five lower fetters they’re reborn spontaneously, because of their passion and love for that meditation. They are extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.

lines.pali: Ayampi kho, gahapati, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena ekadhammo sammadakkhāto, yattha bhikkhuno appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato avimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ vimuccati aparikkhīṇā vā āsavā parikkhayaṁ gacchanti, ananuppattaṁ vā anuttaraṁ yogakkhemaṁ anupāpuṇāti.
lines.sujato: This too is one thing that has been rightly explained by the Blessed One—who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha—practicing which a diligent, keen, and resolute mendicant’s mind is freed, their defilements are ended, and they arrive at the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

below.pali: Puna caparaṁ, gahapati, bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati tathā dutiyaṁ tathā tatiyaṁ tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
below.sujato: Furthermore, a mendicant meditates spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.
below.english: “Then again, a monk keeps pervading the first direction with an awareness imbued with good will, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, & all around, everywhere, in its entirety, he keeps pervading the all-encompassing cosmos with an awareness imbued with good will—abundant, expansive, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill will.

above.pali: Manomayassapi kho ahaṁ, poṭṭhapāda, attapaṭilābhassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desemi:
above.english: “I also teach the Dhamma for the abandoning of the mind-made appropriation of a self…

lines.pali: ‘yathāpaṭipannānaṁ vo saṅkilesikā dhammā pahīyissanti, vodāniyā dhammā abhivaḍḍhissanti, paññāpāripūriṁ vepullattañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissathā’ti.
Siyā kho pana te, poṭṭhapāda, evamassa:
‘saṅkilesikā dhammā pahīyissanti, vodāniyā dhammā abhivaḍḍhissanti, paññāpāripūriṁ vepullattañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati, dukkho ca kho vihāro’ti.
Na kho panetaṁ, poṭṭhapāda, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.

Saṅkilesikā ceva dhammā pahīyissanti, vodāniyā ca dhammā abhivaḍḍhissanti, paññāpāripūriṁ vepullattañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati, pāmujjañceva bhavissati pīti ca passaddhi ca sati ca sampajaññañca sukho ca vihāro.

below.pali: Arūpassapi kho ahaṁ, poṭṭhapāda, attapaṭilābhassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desemi:
below.english: for the abandoning of the formless appropriation of a self,

above.pali: ‘yathāpaṭipannānaṁ vo saṅkilesikā dhammā pahīyissanti, vodāniyā dhammā abhivaḍḍhissanti, paññāpāripūriṁ vepullattañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissathā’ti.
above.english: such that, when you practice it, defiling mental qualities will be abandoned, bright mental qualities will grow, and you will enter & remain in the culmination & abundance of discernment, having known & realized it for yourself in the here & now.…

lines.pali: Siyā kho pana te, poṭṭhapāda, evamassa:
‘saṅkilesikā dhammā pahīyissanti, vodāniyā dhammā abhivaḍḍhissanti, paññāpāripūriṁ vepullattañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati, dukkho ca kho vihāro’ti.
Na kho panetaṁ, poṭṭhapāda, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.

below.pali: Saṅkilesikā ceva dhammā pahīyissanti, vodāniyā ca dhammā abhivaḍḍhissanti, paññāpāripūriṁ vepullattañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati, pāmujjañceva bhavissati pīti ca passaddhi ca sati ca sampajaññañca sukho ca vihāro.
below.english: When defiling mental qualities are abandoned and bright mental qualities have grown, and one enters & remains in the culmination & abundance of discernment, having known & realized it for oneself in the here & now, there is joy, rapture, calm, mindfulness, alertness, and a pleasant/happy abiding.

above.pali: ‘katamo pana so, āvuso, manomayo attapaṭilābho, yassa tumhe pahānāya dhammaṁ desetha, yathāpaṭipannānaṁ vo saṅkilesikā dhammā pahīyissanti, vodāniyā dhammā abhivaḍḍhissanti, paññāpāripūriṁ vepullattañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissathā’ti?
above.sujato: ‘But reverends, what is that mind-made incarnation?’ We’d answer like this,
above.english: ‘What, friend, is the mind-made appropriation of a self…

lines.pali: Tesaṁ mayaṁ evaṁ puṭṭhā evaṁ byākareyyāma:

‘ayaṁ vā so, āvuso, manomayo attapaṭilābho yassa mayaṁ pahānāya dhammaṁ desema, yathāpaṭipannānaṁ vo saṅkilesikā dhammā pahīyissanti, vodāniyā dhammā abhivaḍḍhissanti, paññāpāripūriṁ vepullattañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissathā’ti.
lines.sujato: ‘This is that mind-made incarnation.’

below.pali: ‘katamo pana so, āvuso, arūpo attapaṭilābho, yassa tumhe pahānāya dhammaṁ desetha, yathāpaṭipannānaṁ vo saṅkilesikā dhammā pahīyissanti, vodāniyā dhammā abhivaḍḍhissanti, paññāpāripūriṁ vepullattañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissathā’ti?
below.sujato: ‘But reverends, what is that formless incarnation?’ We’d answer like this,
below.english: the formless appropriation of a self for whose abandoning you teach the Dhamma…?’ When asked this, I would answer,

above.pali: “Sace maṁ, bhante, evaṁ puccheyyuṁ:
above.sujato: “Sir, if they were to ask me this,
above.english: “… Thus asked, lord,

lines.pali: ‘ahosi tvaṁ atītamaddhānaṁ, na tvaṁ na ahosi;
bhavissasi tvaṁ anāgatamaddhānaṁ, na tvaṁ na bhavissasi;
atthi tvaṁ etarahi, na tvaṁ natthī’ti.

below.pali: Evaṁ puṭṭho ahaṁ, bhante, evaṁ byākareyyaṁ:
below.sujato: I’d answer like this,
below.english: I would answer:

above.pali: “Sace pana maṁ, bhante, evaṁ puccheyyuṁ:
above.sujato: “Sir, if they were to ask me this,
above.english: “…Thus asked, lord,

lines.pali: ‘yo te ahosi atīto attapaṭilābho, sova te attapaṭilābho sacco, mogho anāgato, mogho paccuppanno.
Yo te bhavissati anāgato attapaṭilābho, sova te attapaṭilābho sacco, mogho atīto, mogho paccuppanno.
Yo te etarahi paccuppanno attapaṭilābho, sova te attapaṭilābho sacco, mogho atīto, mogho anāgato’ti.

below.pali: Evaṁ puṭṭho ahaṁ, bhante, evaṁ byākareyyaṁ:

above.sujato: For a second time, Kevaḍḍha made the same request,
above.english: A second time.…

lines.pali: “nāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavantaṁ dhaṁsemi;
lines.sujato: “Sir, I am not teaching you the Dhamma,

lines.pali: api ca evaṁ vadāmi:
lines.sujato: but nonetheless I say:

lines.pali: ‘ayaṁ, bhante, nāḷandā iddhā ceva phītā ca bahujanā ākiṇṇamanussā bhagavati abhippasannā.
lines.sujato: ‘Sir, this Nāḷandā is successful and prosperous, populous and full of people.

lines.pali: Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā ekaṁ bhikkhuṁ samādisatu, yo uttari manussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṁ karissati;
lines.sujato: Please direct a mendicant to perform a superhuman demonstration of psychic power.

lines.pali: evāyaṁ nāḷandā bhiyyoso mattāya bhagavati abhippasīdissatī’”ti.
lines.sujato: Then Nāḷandā will become even more devoted to the Buddha!’”

lines.pali: Dutiyampi kho bhagavā kevaṭṭaṁ gahapatiputtaṁ etadavoca:
lines.sujato: But for a second time, the Buddha gave the same answer.

lines.pali: “na kho ahaṁ, kevaṭṭa, bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ dhammaṁ desemi:
‘etha tumhe, bhikkhave, gihīnaṁ odātavasanānaṁ uttari manussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṁ karothā’”ti.

below.pali: Tatiyampi kho kevaṭṭo gahapatiputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
below.sujato: For a third time, Kevaḍḍha made the same request,
below.english: A third time, Kevaṭṭa the householder said to the Blessed One:

above.pali: Ekamidāhaṁ, ānanda, samayaṁ idheva vesāliyaṁ viharāmi udene cetiye.
above.sujato: Ānanda, this one time I was staying right here near Vesālī, at the Udena Shrine …
above.english: “On one occasion, Ānanda, I was staying right here in Vesālī at the Udena shrine…

lines.pali: Tatrāpi kho tāhaṁ, ānanda, āmantesiṁ:
‘ramaṇīyā, ānanda, vesālī, ramaṇīyaṁ udenaṁ cetiyaṁ.
Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṁ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṁ vā.
Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṁ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṁ vā’ti.
Evampi kho tvaṁ, ānanda, tathāgatena oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṁ, na tathāgataṁ yāci:
‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṁ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṁ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānan’ti.
Sace tvaṁ, ānanda, tathāgataṁ yāceyyāsi, dveva te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṁ adhivāseyya, tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṁ dukkaṭaṁ, tuyhevetaṁ aparaddhaṁ.

below.pali: Ekamidāhaṁ, ānanda, samayaṁ idheva vesāliyaṁ viharāmi gotamake cetiye …pe…
below.sujato: at the Gotamaka Shrine …
below.english: the Gotamaka shrine…

above.pali: ayaṁ dhammo ayaṁ vinayo idaṁ satthusāsanan’ti.
above.sujato: this is the teaching, this is the training, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’
above.english: This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

lines.pali: Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṁ neva abhinanditabbaṁ nappaṭikkositabbaṁ.
lines.sujato: You should neither approve nor reject that mendicant’s statement.

lines.pali: “sutaṁ metaṁ, bho ānanda, paribbājakānaṁ vuḍḍhānaṁ mahallakānaṁ ācariyapācariyānaṁ bhāsamānānaṁ:

evaṁ pasanno ahaṁ samaṇe gotame, ‘pahoti me samaṇo gotamo tathā dhammaṁ desetuṁ, yathāhaṁ imaṁ kaṅkhādhammaṁ pajaheyyan’ti.

lines.pali: “bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṁ parinibbuto”ti.

lines.sujato: “The Buddha was an aristocrat and so are we. We too deserve a share of the Buddha’s relics. We will build a monument for them and conduct a memorial service.”

above.sujato: And how does a mendicant do this?
above.english: And how does a monk live with himself as his island, himself as his refuge, with nothing else as his refuge; with the Dhamma as his island, the Dhamma as his refuge, with nothing else as his refuge?

above.english: ‘How is it, friends? Is it the case that “after death a Tathāgata does not exist…”…

above.pali: Tatra, cunda, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṁvādino evaṁdiṭṭhino:

above.english: “Just now, lord, after the meal, on returning from our alms round, we were sitting gathered together here at the pavilion when this discussion arose: [They repeat what had been said.]”

below.sujato: “Mendicants, it is not appropriate for you gentlemen who have gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness to talk about such things.

above.pali: ‘aho vata ahameva ārāmagatānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseyyaṁ, na añño bhikkhu ārāmagatānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseyyā’ti.
above.sujato: ‘Oh, I hope that I might teach the Dhamma to the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen in the monastery, not some other mendicant.’
above.english: ‘O, may I alone, and not another monk, teach the Dhamma to monks…

lines.pali: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, āvuso, vijjati yaṁ añño bhikkhu ārāmagatānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseyya, na so bhikkhu ārāmagatānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseyya.
‘Añño bhikkhu ārāmagatānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti, nāhaṁ ārāmagatānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ desemī’ti—
iti so kupito hoti appatīto.
Yo ceva kho, āvuso, kopo yo ca appaccayo—
ubhayametaṁ aṅgaṇaṁ.

below.pali: ‘aho vata ahameva ārāmagatānaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ dhammaṁ deseyyaṁ …pe…

above.sujato: But it’s possible that some other mendicant teaches the Dhamma …

above.sujato: ‘Oh, I hope that the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen will honor, respect, revere, and venerate me alone, not some other mendicant.’

above.pali: Sa kho so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkileso’ti—iti viditvā abhijjhāvisamalobhaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;
above.sujato: A mendicant who understands that covetousness and immoral greed are corruptions of the mind gives them up.
above.english: “Knowing, ‘Possessiveness-and-inordinate-greed is a defilement of the mind,’ a monk abandons possessiveness-and-inordinate-greed as a defilement of the mind. …

lines.pali: ‘byāpādo cittassa upakkileso’ti—
lines.sujato: A mendicant who understands that ill will …

lines.pali: iti viditvā byāpādaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;
‘kodho cittassa upakkileso’ti—
iti viditvā kodhaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;
‘upanāho cittassa upakkileso’ti—
iti viditvā upanāhaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;
‘makkho cittassa upakkileso’ti—
iti viditvā makkhaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;
‘paḷāso cittassa upakkileso’ti—
iti viditvā paḷāsaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;
‘issā cittassa upakkileso’ti—
iti viditvā issaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;
‘macchariyaṁ cittassa upakkileso’ti—
iti viditvā macchariyaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;
‘māyā cittassa upakkileso’ti—
iti viditvā māyaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;
‘sāṭheyyaṁ cittassa upakkileso’ti—
iti viditvā sāṭheyyaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;
‘thambho cittassa upakkileso’ti—
iti viditvā thambhaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;
‘sārambho cittassa upakkileso’ti—
iti viditvā sārambhaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;
‘māno cittassa upakkileso’ti—
iti viditvā mānaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;
‘atimāno cittassa upakkileso’ti—
iti viditvā atimānaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;
‘mado cittassa upakkileso’ti—
iti viditvā madaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati;

below.pali: ‘pamādo cittassa upakkileso’ti—
below.sujato: negligence is a corruption of the mind gives it up.
below.english: Knowing, ‘Heedlessness is a defilement of the mind,’ a monk abandons heedlessness as a defilement of the mind.

above.pali: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkileso’ti—iti viditvā abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti,
above.sujato: When they have understood these corruptions of the mind
above.english: “When a monk, knowing, ‘Possessiveness-and-inordinate-greed is a defilement of the mind,’ has abandoned possessiveness-and-inordinate-greed as a defilement of the mind… and knowing, ‘Heedlessness is a defilement of the mind,’ has abandoned heedlessness as a defilement of the mind,

lines.pali: ‘byāpādo cittassa upakkileso’ti—
lines.sujato: for what they are, and have given them up,
