below.pali: So buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti:
below.sujato: they have experiential confidence in the Buddha:
below.english: he is endowed with confirmed conviction in the Awakened One:

above.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu seyyathāpi passeyya sarīraṁ sivathikāya chaḍḍitaṁ kākehi vā khajjamānaṁ kulalehi vā khajjamānaṁ gijjhehi vā khajjamānaṁ kaṅkehi vā khajjamānaṁ sunakhehi vā khajjamānaṁ byagghehi vā khajjamānaṁ dīpīhi vā khajjamānaṁ siṅgālehi vā khajjamānaṁ vividhehi vā pāṇakajātehi khajjamānaṁ.
above.sujato: Furthermore, suppose they were to see a corpse discarded in a charnel ground being devoured by crows, hawks, vultures, herons, hounds, tigers, leopards, jackals, and many kinds of little creatures.
above.english: “Or again, as if he were to see a corpse cast away in a charnel ground, being chewed by crows, being chewed by vultures, being chewed by hawks, being chewed by dogs, being chewed by hyenas, being chewed by various other creatures…

lines.pali: So imameva kāyaṁ upasaṁharati:
lines.sujato: They’d compare it with their own body:

lines.pali: ‘ayampi kho kāyo evaṁdhammo evaṁbhāvī evaṁanatīto’ti.
lines.sujato: ‘This body is also of that same nature, that same kind, and cannot go beyond that.’

lines.pali: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati …pe…
lines.sujato: And so they meditate observing an aspect of the body internally …

below.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu seyyathāpi passeyya sarīraṁ sivathikāya chaḍḍitaṁ aṭṭhikasaṅkhalikaṁ samaṁsalohitaṁ nhārusambandhaṁ …pe…
below.sujato: Furthermore, suppose they were to see a corpse discarded in a charnel ground, a skeleton with flesh and blood, held together by sinews …
below.english: a skeleton smeared with flesh & blood, connected with tendons…

above.pali: Aṭṭhikāni apagatasambandhāni disā vidisā vikkhittāni, aññena hatthaṭṭhikaṁ aññena pādaṭṭhikaṁ aññena gopphakaṭṭhikaṁ aññena jaṅghaṭṭhikaṁ aññena ūruṭṭhikaṁ aññena kaṭiṭṭhikaṁ aññena phāsukaṭṭhikaṁ aññena piṭṭhiṭṭhikaṁ aññena khandhaṭṭhikaṁ aññena gīvaṭṭhikaṁ aññena hanukaṭṭhikaṁ aññena dantaṭṭhikaṁ aññena sīsakaṭāhaṁ.
above.sujato: Bones rid of sinews scattered in every direction. Here a hand-bone, there a foot-bone, here an ankle bone, there a shin-bone, here a thigh-bone, there a hip-bone, here a rib-bone, there a back-bone, here an arm-bone, there a neck-bone, here a jaw-bone, there a tooth, here the skull. …
above.english: bones detached from their tendons, scattered in all directions—here a hand bone, there a foot bone, here a shin bone, there a thigh bone, here a hip bone, there a back bone, here a rib, there a chest bone, here a shoulder bone, there a neck bone, here a jaw bone, there a tooth, here a skull…

lines.pali: So imameva kāyaṁ upasaṁharati:
‘ayampi kho kāyo evaṁdhammo evaṁbhāvī evaṁanatīto’ti.
Iti ajjhattaṁ vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati …pe…
evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati.

below.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu seyyathāpi passeyya sarīraṁ sivathikāya chaḍḍitaṁ, aṭṭhikāni setāni saṅkhavaṇṇapaṭibhāgāni …pe…
below.sujato: White bones, the color of shells …
below.english: the bones whitened, somewhat like the color of shells…

above.pali: Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, ime cattāro satipaṭṭhāne evaṁ bhāveyya satta māsāni, tassa dvinnaṁ phalānaṁ aññataraṁ phalaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ
above.sujato: seven months …
above.english: seven months…

lines.pali: diṭṭheva dhamme aññā; sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā.
Tiṭṭhantu, bhikkhave, satta māsāni.

below.pali: Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, ime cattāro satipaṭṭhāne evaṁ bhāveyya cha māsāni …pe…
below.sujato: six months …
below.english: six months…

above.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma āsītikapabbāni vā kāḷapabbāni vā; evamevassu me aṅgapaccaṅgāni bhavanti tāyevappāhāratāya.
above.english: Simply from my eating so little, my limbs became like the jointed segments of vine stems or bamboo stems. …

lines.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma oṭṭhapadaṁ; evamevassu me ānisadaṁ hoti tāyevappāhāratāya.
Seyyathāpi nāma vaṭṭanāvaḷī; evamevassu me piṭṭhikaṇṭako unnatāvanato hoti tāyevappāhāratāya.
Seyyathāpi nāma jarasālāya gopānasiyo oluggaviluggā bhavanti; evamevassu me phāsuḷiyo oluggaviluggā bhavanti tāyevappāhāratāya.
Seyyathāpi nāma gambhīre udapāne udakatārakā gambhīragatā okkhāyikā dissanti; evamevassu me akkhikūpesu akkhitārakā gambhīragatā okkhāyikā dissanti tāyevappāhāratāya.
Seyyathāpi nāma tittakālābu āmakacchinno vātātapena samphuṭito hoti sammilāto; evamevassu me sīsacchavi samphuṭitā hoti sammilātā tāyevappāhāratāya.

So kho ahaṁ, sāriputta, ‘udaracchaviṁ parimasissāmī’ti piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṁyeva pariggaṇhāmi, ‘piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṁ parimasissāmī’ti udaracchaviṁyeva pariggaṇhāmi. Yāvassu me, sāriputta, udaracchavi piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṁ allīnā hoti tāyevappāhāratāya.
So kho ahaṁ, sāriputta, ‘vaccaṁ vā muttaṁ vā karissāmī’ti tattheva avakujjo papatāmi tāyevappāhāratāya.
So kho ahaṁ, sāriputta, tameva kāyaṁ assāsento pāṇinā gattāni anomajjāmi. Tassa mayhaṁ, sāriputta, pāṇinā gattāni anomajjato pūtimūlāni lomāni kāyasmā patanti tāyevappāhāratāya.
lines.sujato: Due to eating so little, when I tried to relieve my body by rubbing my limbs with my hands, the hair, rotted at its roots, fell out.

below.pali: Tāyapi kho ahaṁ, sāriputta, iriyāya tāya paṭipadāya tāya dukkarakārikāya nājjhagamaṁ uttariṁ manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṁ.
below.sujato: But Sāriputta, I did not achieve any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones by that conduct, that practice, that grueling work.
below.english: “But with this racking practice of austerities I didn’t attain any superior human state, any distinction in knowledge or vision worthy of the noble ones.

above.pali: Atha kho te bhikkhū sāvatthiyaṁ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
above.sujato: Then, after the meal, when they returned from almsround, they went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. The Buddha said:
above.english: Then, having gone for alms in Sāvatthī, after their meal, returning from their alms round, the monks went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, having bowed down to him, sat to one side. As they were sitting there, they [told him what had happened].

lines.pali: “idha mayaṁ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṁ piṇḍāya pāvisimha.
Tesaṁ no, bhante, amhākaṁ etadahosi:
‘atippago kho tāva sāvatthiyaṁ piṇḍāya carituṁ,
yaṁ nūna mayaṁ yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ ārāmo tenupasaṅkameyyāmā’ti.
Atha kho mayaṁ, bhante, yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ ārāmo tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṁ sammodimha;
sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdimha. Ekamantaṁ nisinne kho amhe, bhante, te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā etadavocuṁ:
‘samaṇo, āvuso, gotamo kāmānaṁ pariññaṁ paññapeti, mayampi kāmānaṁ pariññaṁ paññapema.
Samaṇo, āvuso, gotamo rūpānaṁ pariññaṁ paññapeti, mayampi rūpānaṁ pariññaṁ paññapema.
Samaṇo, āvuso, gotamo vedanānaṁ pariññaṁ paññapeti, mayampi vedanānaṁ pariññaṁ paññapema.
Idha no, āvuso, ko viseso, ko adhippayāso, kiṁ nānākaraṇaṁ samaṇassa vā gotamassa amhākaṁ vā, yadidaṁ dhammadesanāya vā dhammadesanaṁ anusāsaniyā vā anusāsanin’ti.
Atha kho mayaṁ, bhante, tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ bhāsitaṁ neva abhinandimha, nappaṭikkosimha;
anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamimha:
‘bhagavato santike etassa bhāsitassa atthaṁ ājānissāmā’”ti.

below.pali: “Evaṁvādino, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā:
below.sujato: “Mendicants, when wanderers of other religions say this, you should say to them:
below.english: “Monks, when the wanderers of other persuasions say this, they are to be told,

above.pali: ‘Addhāyasmantehi nigaṇṭhehi sahasā appaṭisaṅkhā vācā bhāsitā:
above.sujato: ‘Clearly the venerables have spoken rashly, without reflection.
above.english: “‘Surely the venerable Nigaṇṭhas said that rashly and without reflecting…

lines.pali: “na kho, āvuso gotama, sukhena sukhaṁ adhigantabbaṁ, dukkhena kho sukhaṁ adhigantabbaṁ;
sukhena cāvuso gotama, sukhaṁ adhigantabbaṁ abhavissa, rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro sukhaṁ adhigaccheyya, rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro sukhavihāritaro āyasmatā gotamenā”ti.

below.pali: Api ca ahameva tattha paṭipucchitabbo:
below.sujato: Rather, I’m the one who should be asked about
below.english: for instead, I should be asked,

above.pali: pañca rattindivāni …
above.sujato: five days …
above.english: for five days & nights…

lines.pali: cattāri rattindivāni …
lines.sujato: four days …

lines.pali: tīṇi rattindivāni …
lines.sujato: three days …

lines.pali: dve rattindivāni …
lines.sujato: two days …

below.pali: ekaṁ rattindivaṁ ekantasukhaṁ paṭisaṁvedī viharitun’ti?
below.sujato: one day?’
below.english: for a day & a night?’

above.pali: Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi:
above.sujato: and told the mendicants what had happened.
above.english: he [told the monks what had happened].

lines.pali: “idhāhaṁ, bhikkhave, pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya kapilavatthuṁ piṇḍāya pāvisiṁ.
Kapilavatthusmiṁ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena mahāvanaṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁ divāvihārāya.
Mahāvanaṁ ajjhogāhetvā beluvalaṭṭhikāya mūle divāvihāraṁ nisīdiṁ.
Daṇḍapāṇipi kho, bhikkhave, sakko jaṅghāvihāraṁ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno yena mahāvanaṁ tenupasaṅkami.
Mahāvanaṁ ajjhogāhetvā yena beluvalaṭṭhikā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mayā saddhiṁ sammodi.
Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā daṇḍamolubbha ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho, bhikkhave, daṇḍapāṇi sakko maṁ etadavoca:
‘kiṁvādī samaṇo kimakkhāyī’ti?

below.pali: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
below.sujato: When he had spoken, one of the mendicants said to him,
below.english: When this was said, a certain monk said to the Blessed One,

above.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etadavocuṁ:
above.sujato: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side. They told him what had happened, and said:
above.english: After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies, they sat to one side. As they were sitting there, they [told him what had happened, and added,]

lines.pali: “idaṁ kho no, āvuso kaccāna, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
‘yatonidānaṁ, bhikkhu, purisaṁ papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācaranti.
Ettha ce natthi abhinanditabbaṁ abhivaditabbaṁ ajjhositabbaṁ.
Esevanto rāgānusayānaṁ …pe…
etthete pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhantī’ti.
Tesaṁ no, āvuso kaccāna, amhākaṁ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi:
‘idaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
“yatonidānaṁ, bhikkhu, purisaṁ papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācaranti.
Ettha ce natthi abhinanditabbaṁ abhivaditabbaṁ ajjhositabbaṁ.
Esevanto rāgānusayānaṁ …pe…
etthete pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhantī”’ti.
Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajeyyāti?
Tesaṁ no, āvuso kaccāna, amhākaṁ etadahosi:

‘ayaṁ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ, pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
Yannūna mayaṁ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāmā’ti.

below.pali: Vibhajatāyasmā mahākaccāno”ti.
below.sujato: “May Venerable Mahākaccāna please explain this.”
below.english: “Analyze the meaning, Ven. Mahā Kaccāna!”

above.pali: Atha kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahākaccānassa bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
above.sujato: Then those mendicants, approving and agreeing with what Mahākaccāna said, rose from their seats and went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened, adding:
above.english: Then the monks, delighting in & approving of Ven. Mahā Kaccāna’s words, got up from their seats and went to the Blessed One. On arrival, having bowed down to him, they sat to one side. As they were sitting there, they [told him what had happened after he had gone into his dwelling, and ended by saying,]

lines.pali: “yaṁ kho no, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
‘yatonidānaṁ, bhikkhu, purisaṁ papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācaranti.
Ettha ce natthi abhinanditabbaṁ abhivaditabbaṁ ajjhositabbaṁ.
Esevanto rāgānusayānaṁ …pe…
etthete pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhantī’ti.
Tesaṁ no, bhante, amhākaṁ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi:
‘idaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
“yatonidānaṁ, bhikkhu, purisaṁ papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācaranti.
Ettha ce natthi abhinanditabbaṁ abhivaditabbaṁ ajjhositabbaṁ.

Esevanto rāgānusayānaṁ, esevanto paṭighānusayānaṁ, esevanto diṭṭhānusayānaṁ, esevanto vicikicchānusayānaṁ, esevanto mānānusayānaṁ, esevanto bhavarāgānusayānaṁ, esevanto avijjānusayānaṁ, esevanto daṇḍādānasatthādānakalahaviggahavivādatuvaṁtuvaṁpesuññamusāvādānaṁ.
Etthete pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhantī”ti.
Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajeyyā’ti?
Tesaṁ no, bhante, amhākaṁ etadahosi:

‘ayaṁ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ, pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ, yannūna mayaṁ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāmā’ti.
Atha kho mayaṁ, bhante, yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipucchimha.

below.pali: Tesaṁ no, bhante, āyasmatā mahākaccānena imehi ākārehi imehi padehi imehi byañjanehi attho vibhatto”ti.
below.sujato: “Mahākaccāna clearly explained the meaning to us in this manner, with these words and phrases.”
below.english: “Then Ven. Mahā Kaccāna analyzed the meaning using these words, these statements, these phrases.”

above.pali: Yato kho te bhikkhū nāsakkhiṁsu ariṭṭhaṁ bhikkhuṁ gaddhabādhipubbaṁ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṁ, atha kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
above.sujato: When they weren’t able to dissuade Ariṭṭha from his view, the mendicants went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.
above.english: So when the monks were unable to pry the monk Ariṭṭha Formerly-of-the-Vulture-Killers away from that evil viewpoint, they went to the Blessed One and on arrival, having bowed down to him, sat to one side. As they were sitting there, they [told him what had happened].

lines.pali: “ariṭṭhassa nāma, bhante, bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ:
‘tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṁ antarāyāyā’ti.
Assumha kho mayaṁ, bhante:
‘ariṭṭhassa kira nāma bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ—
tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṁ antarāyāyā’ti.

below.pali: Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ āmantesi:
below.sujato: So the Buddha addressed one of the monks,
below.english: So the Blessed One told a certain monk,

above.english: The second herd of deer…

evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṁsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā.

below.pali: Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭiviramiṁsu …pe…

Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭiviramiṁsu …pe…
evañhi te dutiyāpi migajātā na parimucciṁsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā.

Yannūna mayaṁ amuṁ nivāpaṁ nivuttaṁ nevāpikassa upanissāya āsayaṁ kappeyyāma, tatrāsayaṁ kappetvā amuṁ nivāpaṁ nivuttaṁ nevāpikassa ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjissāma, ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṁ āpajjissāma, amattā samānā na pamādaṁ āpajjissāma, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavissāma nevāpikassa amusmiṁ nivāpe”ti.

below.pali: Te amuṁ nivāpaṁ nivuttaṁ nevāpikassa upanissāya āsayaṁ kappayiṁsu, tatrāsayaṁ kappetvā amuṁ nivāpaṁ nivuttaṁ nevāpikassa ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṁsu, te tattha ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṁ āpajjiṁsu, amattā samānā na pamādaṁ āpajjiṁsu, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṁ nevāpikassa amusmiṁ nivāpe.
below.english: took up residence near where poison-grass had been sown by the poison-grass sower and—having taken up residence there—ate food without venturing unwarily into the poison-grass sown by the poison-grass sower.…

lines.pali: Tatra nevāpikassa ca nevāpikaparisāya ca etadahosi:
“saṭhāssunāmime tatiyā migajātā ketabino, iddhimantāssunāmime tatiyā migajātā parajanā, imañca nāma nivāpaṁ nivuttaṁ paribhuñjanti.
Na ca nesaṁ jānāma āgatiṁ vā gatiṁ vā.
Yannūna mayaṁ imaṁ nivāpaṁ nivuttaṁ mahatīhi daṇḍavākarāhi samantā sappadesaṁ anuparivāreyyāma, appeva nāma tatiyānaṁ migajātānaṁ āsayaṁ passeyyāma, yattha te gāhaṁ gaccheyyun”ti.

below.pali: Te amuṁ nivāpaṁ nivuttaṁ mahatīhi daṇḍavākarāhi samantā sappadesaṁ anuparivāresuṁ.
below.english: But the poison-grass sower & his followers… had the sown poison-grass surrounded on all sides over a large area with stick snares.

above.pali: Yepi te dutiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṁ samacintesuṁ:
above.sujato: and second groups of ascetics and brahmins …
above.english: “‘The second group of contemplatives & brahmans…

below.pali: Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā lokāmisā paṭiviramiṁsu.
below.english: entirely avoided that poison-grass food, the baits of the world.

above.pali: Tesaṁ adhimattakasimānaṁ pattakāyānaṁ balavīriyaṁ parihāyi, balavīriye parihīne cetovimutti parihāyi, cetovimuttiyā parihīnāya tameva nivāpaṁ nivuttaṁ mārassa paccāgamiṁsu tāni ca lokāmisāni.
above.english: Having lost their strength & energy, they lost their awareness-release. Having lost their awareness-release, they returned to the poison-grass & baits of the world sown by Māra.…

lines.pali: Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṁsu.
Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṁ āpajjiṁsu, mattā samānā pamādaṁ āpajjiṁsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṁ mārassa amusmiṁ nivāpe amusmiñca lokāmise.

below.pali: Evañhi te dutiyāpi samaṇabrāhmaṇā na parimucciṁsu mārassa iddhānubhāvā.
below.sujato: failed to get free of Māra’s power.
below.english: That’s why that second group of contemplatives & brahmans didn’t escape from Māra’s power & control.

Appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṁ mārassa amusmiṁ nivāpe amusmiñca lokāmise.

above.sujato: Partners and children, male and female bondservants, goats and sheep, chickens and pigs, elephants and cattle, and gold and currency are liable to grow old.
above.english: Spouses & children… men & women slaves… goats & sheep… fowl & pigs… elephants, cattle, horses, & mares… gold & silver are subject to aging…

lines.pali: Jarādhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo.
lines.sujato: These attachments are liable to grow old.

lines.pali: Etthāyaṁ gathito mucchito ajjhāpanno attanā jarādhammo samāno jarādhammaṁyeva pariyesati.
lines.sujato: Someone who is tied, infatuated, and attached to such things, themselves liable to grow old, seeks what is also liable to grow old.

above.pali: “mayhampi, bhante, evaṁ hoti:
above.english: “Here, lord, the thought occurs to me also, ‘It’s a gain for me, a great gain…

lines.pali: ‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṁ vata me,
yohaṁ evarūpehi sabrahmacārīhi saddhiṁ viharāmī’ti.
Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, imesu āyasmantesu mettaṁ kāyakammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ āvi ceva raho ca,
mettaṁ vacīkammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ āvi ceva raho ca,
mettaṁ manokammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ āvi ceva raho ca.
Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, evaṁ hoti:
‘yannūnāhaṁ sakaṁ cittaṁ nikkhipitvā imesaṁyeva āyasmantānaṁ cittassa vasena vatteyyan’ti.
So kho ahaṁ, bhante, sakaṁ cittaṁ nikkhipitvā imesaṁyeva āyasmantānaṁ cittassa vasena vattāmi.

below.pali: Nānā hi kho no, bhante, kāyā ekañca pana maññe cittan”ti.
below.english: We are separate in body, lord, but one—as it were—in mind.”

above.pali: Imesampi hi, bho gotama, saṅghānaṁ gaṇānaṁ—
above.sujato: Even federations such as the
above.english: Even these oligarchic groups, such as the Vajjians & Mallans, wield the power in their own domains

lines.pali: Seyyathidaṁ—vajjīnaṁ mallānaṁ—
lines.sujato: Vajjis and Mallas

lines.pali: vattati sakasmiṁ vijite vaso—
lines.sujato: have such power in their own realm.

below.pali: ghātetāyaṁ vā ghātetuṁ, jāpetāyaṁ vā jāpetuṁ, pabbājetāyaṁ vā pabbājetuṁ.
below.english: to execute those (they’ve) sentenced to be executed, to fine those (they’ve) sentenced to be fined, or to banish those (they’ve) sentenced to be banished,

above.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma kammāragaggariyā dhamamānāya adhimatto saddo hoti;
above.sujato: like the puffing of a blacksmith’s bellows.
above.english: just like the loud roar of winds coming out of a smith’s bellows.…

lines.pali: evameva kho me, aggivessana, mukhato ca nāsato ca assāsapassāsesu uparuddhesu kaṇṇasotehi vātānaṁ nikkhamantānaṁ adhimatto saddo hoti.
Āraddhaṁ kho pana me, aggivessana, vīriyaṁ hoti asallīnaṁ upaṭṭhitā sati asammuṭṭhā. Sāraddho ca pana me kāyo hoti appaṭippassaddho teneva dukkhappadhānena padhānābhitunnassa sato.
lines.sujato: My energy was roused up and unflagging, and my mindfulness was established and lucid, but my body was disturbed, not tranquil, because I’d pushed too hard with that painful striving.

lines.pali: Evarūpāpi kho me, aggivessana, uppannā dukkhā vedanā cittaṁ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati.
lines.sujato: But even such painful feeling did not occupy my mind.

below.pali: So kho ahaṁ, aggivessana, mukhato ca nāsato ca kaṇṇato ca assāsapassāse uparundhiṁ.
below.sujato: So I cut off my breathing through my mouth and nose and ears.
below.english: So I stopped the in-breaths & out-breaths in my nose & mouth & ears.

above.pali: Seyyathāpi, aggivessana, balavā puriso tiṇhena sikharena muddhani abhimattheyya;
above.sujato: like a strong man was drilling into my head with a sharp point.
above.english: just as if a strong man were slicing my head open with a sharp sword.…

lines.pali: evameva kho me, aggivessana, mukhato ca nāsato ca kaṇṇato ca assāsapassāsesu uparuddhesu adhimattā vātā muddhani ūhananti.
Āraddhaṁ kho pana me, aggivessana, vīriyaṁ hoti asallīnaṁ upaṭṭhitā sati asammuṭṭhā. Sāraddho ca pana me kāyo hoti appaṭippassaddho teneva dukkhappadhānena padhānābhitunnassa sato.
lines.sujato: My energy was roused up and unflagging, and my mindfulness was established and lucid, but my body was disturbed, not tranquil, because I’d pushed too hard with that painful striving.

lines.pali: Evarūpāpi kho me, aggivessana, uppannā dukkhā vedanā cittaṁ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati.
lines.sujato: But even such painful feeling did not occupy my mind.

below.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, aggivessana, mukhato ca nāsato ca kaṇṇato ca assāsapassāsesu uparuddhesu adhimattā sīse sīsavedanā honti.
below.sujato: But then I got a severe headache,
below.english: Extreme pains arose in my head,

above.pali: Seyyathāpi, aggivessana, balavā puriso daḷhena varattakkhaṇḍena sīse sīsaveṭhaṁ dadeyya;
above.sujato: like a strong man was tightening a strong leather strap around my head.
above.english: just as if a strong man were tightening a turban made of tough leather straps around my head.…

lines.pali: evameva kho me, aggivessana, mukhato ca nāsato ca kaṇṇato ca assāsapassāsesu uparuddhesu adhimattā sīse sīsavedanā honti.

below.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, aggivessana, mukhato ca nāsato ca kaṇṇato ca assāsapassāsesu uparuddhesu adhimattā vātā kucchiṁ parikantanti.
below.sujato: But then strong winds carved up my belly,
below.english: Extreme forces carved up my stomach cavity,

above.pali: Seyyathāpi, aggivessana, dakkho goghātako vā goghātakantevāsī vā tiṇhena govikantanena kucchiṁ parikanteyya;
above.sujato: like a deft butcher or their apprentice was slicing my belly open with a sharp meat cleaver.
above.english: just as if a butcher or his apprentice were to carve up the stomach cavity of an ox.…

lines.pali: evameva kho me, aggivessana, mukhato ca nāsato ca kaṇṇato ca assāsapassāsesu uparuddhesu adhimattā vātā kucchiṁ parikantanti.
Āraddhaṁ kho pana me, aggivessana, vīriyaṁ hoti asallīnaṁ upaṭṭhitā sati asammuṭṭhā. Sāraddho ca pana me kāyo hoti appaṭippassaddho teneva dukkhappadhānena padhānābhitunnassa sato.

lines.sujato: But even such painful feeling did not occupy my mind.

below.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, aggivessana, mukhato ca nāsato ca kaṇṇato ca assāsapassāsesu uparuddhesu adhimatto kāyasmiṁ ḍāho hoti.
below.sujato: But then there was a severe burning in my body,
below.english: There was an extreme burning in my body,

above.pali: Yato kho te bhikkhū nāsakkhiṁsu sātiṁ bhikkhuṁ kevaṭṭaputtaṁ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṁ, atha kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
above.sujato: When they weren’t able to dissuade Sāti from his view, the mendicants went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.
above.english: So when the monks were unable to pry the monk Sāti the Fisherman’s Son away from that evil viewpoint, they went to the Blessed One and on arrival, having bowed down to him, sat to one side. As they were sitting there, they (told him what had happened).

lines.pali: “sātissa nāma, bhante, bhikkhuno kevaṭṭaputtassa evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ:
‘tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṁ viññāṇaṁ sandhāvati saṁsarati, anaññan’ti.
Assumha kho mayaṁ, bhante, sātissa kira nāma bhikkhuno kevaṭṭaputtassa evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ:
‘tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṁ viññāṇaṁ sandhāvati saṁsarati, anaññan’ti.
Atha kho mayaṁ, bhante, yena sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā sātiṁ bhikkhuṁ kevaṭṭaputtaṁ etadavocumha:
‘saccaṁ kira te, āvuso sāti, evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ:
“tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṁ viññāṇaṁ sandhāvati saṁsarati, anaññan”’ti?
Evaṁ vutte, bhante, sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto amhe etadavoca:
‘evaṁ byā kho ahaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṁ viññāṇaṁ sandhāvati saṁsarati, anaññan’ti.
Atha kho mayaṁ, bhante, sātiṁ bhikkhuṁ kevaṭṭaputtaṁ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetukāmā samanuyuñjimha samanugāhimha samanubhāsimha:
‘mā evaṁ, āvuso sāti, avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.
Anekapariyāyenāvuso sāti, paṭiccasamuppannaṁ viññāṇaṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā, aññatra paccayā natthi viññāṇassa sambhavo’ti.
Evampi kho, bhante, sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto amhehi samanuyuñjiyamāno samanugāhiyamāno samanubhāsiyamāno tadeva pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ thāmasā parāmasā abhinivissa voharati:
‘evaṁ byā kho ahaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṁ viññāṇaṁ sandhāvati saṁsarati, anaññan’ti.
Yato kho mayaṁ, bhante, nāsakkhimha sātiṁ bhikkhuṁ kevaṭṭaputtaṁ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṁ, atha mayaṁ etamatthaṁ bhagavato ārocemā”ti.

below.pali: Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ āmantesi:
below.sujato: So the Buddha addressed one of the monks,
below.english: So the Blessed One told a certain monk,

above.pali: Tāya ca pana parisuddhavacīsamācāratāya nevattānukkaṁsessāma na paraṁ vambhessāmā’ti evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṁ.
above.english: We will not exalt ourselves nor disparage others on account of that pure verbal…

lines.pali: Siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, tumhākaṁ evamassa:
‘hirottappenamha samannāgatā, parisuddho no kāyasamācāro, parisuddho vacīsamācāro;
alamettāvatā katamettāvatā, anuppatto no sāmaññattho, natthi no kiñci uttariṁ karaṇīyan’ti tāvatakeneva tuṭṭhiṁ āpajjeyyātha.
Ārocayāmi vo, bhikkhave, paṭivedayāmi vo, bhikkhave:
‘mā vo sāmaññatthikānaṁ sataṁ sāmaññattho parihāyi, sati uttariṁ karaṇīye’.
Kiñca, bhikkhave, uttariṁ karaṇīyaṁ?

below.pali: ‘Parisuddho no manosamācāro bhavissati uttāno vivaṭo na ca chiddavā saṁvuto ca.
below.sujato: mental behavior …
below.english: mental conduct’:

above.pali: brahmakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti;
above.sujato: the gods of the Divinity’s host …
above.english: “If one—a person of Dhamma conduct, harmonious conduct—should wish: ‘O if I, with the break-up of the body, after death, were to reappear among the devas in Brahmā’s retinue…

Taṁ kissa hetu?
Tathā hi so dhammacārī samacārī.
Ākaṅkheyya ce, gahapatayo, dhammacārī samacārī:

below.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā ābhānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti;
below.sujato: the luminous gods …
below.english: the Radiant devas…

above.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā ābhānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti;
above.sujato: the luminous gods …
above.english: the Radiant devas…

Tathā hi so dhammacārī samacārī.

above.sujato: third absorption …
above.english: third,

anuttaraṁ yogakkhemaṁ anupāpuṇāti.

above.sujato: fourth absorption …

‘idampi kho catutthaṁ jhānaṁ abhisaṅkhataṁ abhisañcetayitaṁ …pe…

below.pali: Puna caparaṁ, gahapati, bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṁ, tathā tatiyaṁ, tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharati.
below.sujato: Furthermore, a mendicant meditates spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.
below.english: “Then again, a monk keeps pervading the first direction [the east] with an awareness imbued with goodwill, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, & all around, everywhere, in its entirety, he keeps pervading the all-encompassing cosmos with an awareness imbued with goodwill—abundant, expansive, unlimited, without hostility, without ill will.

above.pali: upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṁ, tathā tatiyaṁ, tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharati.

lines.pali: So iti paṭisañcikkhati:
‘ayampi kho upekkhācetovimutti abhisaṅkhatā abhisañcetayitā.
Yaṁ kho pana kiñci abhisaṅkhataṁ abhisañcetayitaṁ tadaniccaṁ nirodhadhamman’ti pajānāti.
So tattha ṭhito …pe…
anuttaraṁ yogakkhemaṁ anupāpuṇāti.

below.pali: Puna caparaṁ, gahapati, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
below.sujato: Furthermore, householder, a mendicant, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.
below.english: “Then again, a monk—with the complete transcending of perceptions of (physical) form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and not attending to perceptions of multiplicity, (perceiving,) ‘Infinite space’—enters & remains in the dimension of the infinitude of space.

above.pali: Puna caparaṁ, gahapati, bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
above.sujato: Furthermore, a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite consciousness. …
above.english: [Similarly with the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness and the dimension of nothingness.]

lines.pali: So iti paṭisañcikkhati:
‘ayampi kho viññāṇañcāyatanasamāpatti abhisaṅkhatā abhisañcetayitā.
Yaṁ kho pana kiñci abhisaṅkhataṁ abhisañcetayitaṁ tadaniccaṁ nirodhadhamman’ti pajānāti.
So tattha ṭhito …pe…
anuttaraṁ yogakkhemaṁ anupāpuṇāti.

below.pali: Evaṁ vutte, dasamo gahapati aṭṭhakanāgaro āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
below.sujato: When he said this, the householder Dasama said to Venerable Ānanda,
below.english: When this was said, Dasama the householder from Aṭṭhakanagara said to Ven. Ānanda,

above.pali: ‘Saccavācaṁ nissāya musāvādo pahātabbo’ti iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ, kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
above.sujato: lying …

lines.pali: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
‘yesaṁ kho ahaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ hetu musāvādī assaṁ, tesāhaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ pahānāya samucchedāya paṭipanno.
Ahañceva kho pana musāvādī assaṁ, attāpi maṁ upavadeyya musāvādapaccayā, anuviccāpi maṁ viññū garaheyyuṁ musāvādapaccayā, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā musāvādapaccayā.
Etadeva kho pana saṁyojanaṁ etaṁ nīvaraṇaṁ yadidaṁ musāvādo.
Ye ca musāvādapaccayā uppajjeyyuṁ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, musāvādā paṭiviratassa evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti’.
‘Saccavācaṁ nissāya musāvādo pahātabbo’ti—
iti yantaṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
‘Apisuṇaṁ vācaṁ nissāya pisuṇā vācā pahātabbā’ti iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ, kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
lines.sujato: backbiting …

lines.pali: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
‘yesaṁ kho ahaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ hetu pisuṇavāco assaṁ, tesāhaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ pahānāya samucchedāya paṭipanno.
Ahañceva kho pana pisuṇavāco assaṁ, attāpi maṁ upavadeyya pisuṇavācāpaccayā, anuviccāpi maṁ viññū garaheyyuṁ pisuṇavācāpaccayā, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā pisuṇavācāpaccayā.
Etadeva kho pana saṁyojanaṁ etaṁ nīvaraṇaṁ yadidaṁ pisuṇā vācā.
Ye ca pisuṇavācāpaccayā uppajjeyyuṁ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭiviratassa evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti’.
‘Apisuṇaṁ vācaṁ nissāya pisuṇā vācā pahātabbā’ti—
iti yantaṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
‘Agiddhilobhaṁ nissāya giddhilobho pahātabbo’ti iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ, kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
lines.sujato: greed and lust …

lines.pali: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
‘yesaṁ kho ahaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ hetu giddhilobhī assaṁ, tesāhaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ pahānāya samucchedāya paṭipanno.
Ahañceva kho pana giddhilobhī assaṁ, attāpi maṁ upavadeyya giddhilobhapaccayā, anuviccāpi maṁ viññū garaheyyuṁ giddhilobhapaccayā, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā giddhilobhapaccayā.
Etadeva kho pana saṁyojanaṁ etaṁ nīvaraṇaṁ yadidaṁ giddhilobho.
Ye ca giddhilobhapaccayā uppajjeyyuṁ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, giddhilobhā paṭiviratassa evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti’.
‘Agiddhilobhaṁ nissāya giddhilobho pahātabbo’ti—
iti yantaṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
‘Anindārosaṁ nissāya nindāroso pahātabbo’ti iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ, kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
lines.sujato: blaming and insulting …

lines.pali: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
‘yesaṁ kho ahaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ hetu nindārosī assaṁ, tesāhaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ pahānāya samucchedāya paṭipanno.
Ahañceva kho pana nindārosī assaṁ, attāpi maṁ upavadeyya nindārosapaccayā, anuviccāpi maṁ viññū garaheyyuṁ nindārosapaccayā, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā nindārosapaccayā.
Etadeva kho pana saṁyojanaṁ etaṁ nīvaraṇaṁ yadidaṁ nindāroso.
Ye ca nindārosapaccayā uppajjeyyuṁ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, anindārosissa evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti’.
‘Anindārosaṁ nissāya nindāroso pahātabbo’ti—
iti yantaṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
‘Akkodhūpāyāsaṁ nissāya kodhūpāyāso pahātabbo’ti iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ, kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
lines.sujato: anger and distress …

lines.pali: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
‘yesaṁ kho ahaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ hetu kodhūpāyāsī assaṁ, tesāhaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ pahānāya samucchedāya paṭipanno.
Ahañceva kho pana kodhūpāyāsī assaṁ, attāpi maṁ upavadeyya kodhūpāyāsapaccayā, anuviccāpi maṁ viññū garaheyyuṁ kodhūpāyāsapaccayā, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā kodhūpāyāsapaccayā.
Etadeva kho pana saṁyojanaṁ etaṁ nīvaraṇaṁ yadidaṁ kodhūpāyāso.
Ye ca kodhūpāyāsapaccayā uppajjeyyuṁ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, akkodhūpāyāsissa evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti’.
‘Akkodhūpāyāsaṁ nissāya kodhūpāyāso pahātabbo’ti—
iti yantaṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.

below.pali: “Seyyathāpi, gahapati, kukkuro jighacchādubbalyapareto goghātakasūnaṁ paccupaṭṭhito assa.
below.sujato: “Householder, suppose a dog weak with hunger was hanging around a butcher’s shop.
below.english: “Suppose a dog, overcome with weakness & hunger, were to come across a slaughterhouse,

above.pali: Dutiyampi kho dīghatapassī nigaṇṭho nigaṇṭhaṁ nāṭaputtaṁ etadavoca:
above.sujato: For a second time …
above.english: A second time…

lines.pali: “saccaṁyeva, bhante …pe…
upālissa gahapatissa sāvakattaṁ upagaccheyyā”ti.

below.pali: Tatiyampi kho dīghatapassī nigaṇṭho nigaṇṭhaṁ nāṭaputtaṁ etadavoca:
below.sujato: and a third time, Dīgha Tapassī told the Jain Ñātika
below.english: A third time, Dīgha Tapassin the Nigaṇṭha said to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta,

above.pali: “Idhāhaṁ, bhante, yena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā nigaṇṭhaṁ nāṭaputtaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁ. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho maṁ, bhante, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto etadavoca:
above.sujato: Then Abhaya told the Buddha all that had happened.
above.english: “Just yesterday, lord, I went to Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta and… he said to me…

lines.pali: ‘ehi tvaṁ, rājakumāra, samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṁ āropehi.
Evaṁ te kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchissati—
abhayena rājakumārena samaṇassa gotamassa evaṁ mahiddhikassa evaṁ mahānubhāvassa vādo āropito’ti.
Evaṁ vutte, ahaṁ, bhante, nigaṇṭhaṁ nāṭaputtaṁ etadavocaṁ:
‘yathā kathaṁ panāhaṁ, bhante, samaṇassa gotamassa evaṁ mahiddhikassa evaṁ mahānubhāvassa vādaṁ āropessāmī’ti?

below.pali: ‘Ehi tvaṁ, rājakumāra, yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā samaṇaṁ gotamaṁ evaṁ vadehi:
below.english: ‘Come now, prince. Go to Gotama the contemplative and on arrival say this:

above.pali: “bhāseyya nu kho, bhante, tathāgato taṁ vācaṁ yā sā vācā paresaṁ appiyā amanāpā”ti?
above.english: “Lord, would the Tathāgata say words that are unendearing & disagreeable to others?”

lines.pali: Sace te samaṇo gotamo evaṁ puṭṭho evaṁ byākaroti:
“bhāseyya, rājakumāra, tathāgato taṁ vācaṁ yā sā vācā paresaṁ appiyā amanāpā”ti, tamenaṁ tvaṁ evaṁ vadeyyāsi:
“atha kiñcarahi te, bhante, puthujjanena nānākaraṇaṁ?
Puthujjanopi hi taṁ vācaṁ bhāseyya yā sā vācā paresaṁ appiyā amanāpā”ti.
Sace pana te samaṇo gotamo evaṁ puṭṭho evaṁ byākaroti:
“na, rājakumāra, tathāgato taṁ vācaṁ bhāseyya yā sā vācā paresaṁ appiyā amanāpā”ti, tamenaṁ tvaṁ evaṁ vadeyyāsi—

below.pali: atha kiñcarahi te, bhante, devadatto byākato:

above.pali: atha kiñcarahi te, bhante, devadatto byākato:

lines.pali: “āpāyiko devadatto, nerayiko devadatto, kappaṭṭho devadatto, atekiccho devadatto”ti?
Tāya ca pana te vācāya devadatto kupito ahosi anattamano’ti.
Imaṁ kho te, rājakumāra, samaṇo gotamo ubhatokoṭikaṁ pañhaṁ puṭṭho samāno neva sakkhiti uggilituṁ na sakkhiti ogilituṁ.

below.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma purisassa ayosiṅghāṭakaṁ kaṇṭhe vilaggaṁ, so neva sakkuṇeyya uggilituṁ na sakkuṇeyya ogilituṁ;
below.english: Just as if a two-horned chestnut were stuck in a man’s throat: He would not be able to swallow it down or spit it up.

above.pali: imā kho, thapati, tisso vedanā vuttā bhagavatā”ti.
above.english: These are the three feelings described by the Blessed One.”

lines.pali: Dutiyampi kho pañcakaṅgo thapati āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ etadavoca:
lines.sujato: For a second time, Pañcakaṅga said to Udāyī,

lines.pali: “na kho, bhante udāyi, tisso vedanā vuttā bhagavatā;
lines.sujato: “The Buddha hasn’t spoken of three feelings,

lines.pali: dve vedanā vuttā bhagavatā—
lines.sujato: he’s spoken of two.”

lines.pali: sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā.
Yāyaṁ, bhante, adukkhamasukhā vedanā santasmiṁ esā paṇīte sukhe vuttā bhagavatā”ti.

below.pali: Tatiyampi kho pañcakaṅgo thapati āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ etadavoca:
below.sujato: And for a third time, Pañcakaṅga said to Udāyī,
below.english: A second time… A third time, Pañcakaṅga the carpenter said to Ven. Udāyin,

above.pali: ‘karoto kārayato, chindato chedāpayato, pacato pācāpayato, socayato socāpayato, kilamato kilamāpayato, phandato phandāpayato, pāṇamatipātayato, adinnaṁ ādiyato, sandhiṁ chindato, nillopaṁ harato, ekāgārikaṁ karoto, paripanthe tiṭṭhato, paradāraṁ gacchato, musā bhaṇato; karoto karīyati pāpaṁ.
above.sujato: the one who acts does a bad deed when they punish, etc.
above.english: ’In acting or getting others to act, in mutilating or getting others to mutilate, in torturing or getting others to torture… one does evil.…

lines.pali: Khurapariyantena cepi cakkena yo imissā pathaviyā pāṇe ekaṁ maṁsakhalaṁ ekaṁ maṁsapuñjaṁ kareyya, atthi tatonidānaṁ pāpaṁ, atthi pāpassa āgamo.
Dakkhiṇañcepi gaṅgāya tīraṁ gaccheyya hananto ghātento, chindanto chedāpento, pacanto pācento, atthi tatonidānaṁ pāpaṁ, atthi pāpassa āgamo.

below.pali: Uttarañcepi gaṅgāya tīraṁ gaccheyya dadanto dāpento, yajanto yajāpento, atthi tatonidānaṁ puññaṁ, atthi puññassa āgamo. Dānena damena saṁyamena saccavajjena atthi puññaṁ, atthi puññassa āgamo’ti
below.english: Through generosity, self-control, restraint, and truthful speech there is merit from that cause, there is a coming of merit’—

above.pali: ‘natthi hetu, natthi paccayo sattānaṁ saṅkilesāya;
above.sujato: there’s no cause or reason for the corruption of sentient beings, etc.
above.english: ’There is no cause, no requisite condition, for the defilement of beings.…

lines.pali: ahetū appaccayā sattā saṅkilissanti.
Natthi hetu, natthi paccayo sattānaṁ visuddhiyā;
ahetū appaccayā sattā visujjhanti.

below.pali: Natthi balaṁ, natthi vīriyaṁ, natthi purisathāmo, natthi purisaparakkamo; sabbe sattā sabbe pāṇā sabbe bhūtā sabbe jīvā avasā abalā avīriyā niyatisaṅgatibhāvapariṇatā chasvevābhijātīsu sukhadukkhaṁ paṭisaṁvedentī’ti
below.english: Subject to the changes of fate, serendipity, and nature, they experience pleasure and pain in the six great classes of birth’—

above.pali: ‘atthi hetu, atthi paccayo sattānaṁ saṅkilesāya;
above.sujato: there is a cause and reason for the corruption of sentient beings, etc.
above.english: ’There is causality, there is requisite condition, for the defilement of beings.…

lines.pali: sahetū sappaccayā sattā saṅkilissanti.
Atthi hetu, atthi paccayo sattānaṁ visuddhiyā;
sahetū sappaccayā sattā visujjhanti.

below.pali: Atthi balaṁ, atthi vīriyaṁ, atthi purisathāmo, atthi purisaparakkamo; na sabbe sattā sabbe pāṇā sabbe bhūtā sabbe jīvā avasā abalā avīriyā niyatisaṅgatibhāvapariṇatā chasvevābhijātīsu sukhadukkhaṁ paṭisaṁvedentī’ti
below.english: It’s not the case that all living beings, all life, all beings, all souls are powerless, devoid of strength, devoid of effort; or that subject to the changes of fate, serendipity, and nature, they experience pleasure and pain in the six great classes of birth’—

above.pali: yānimāni diṭṭhigatāni bhagavatā abyākatāni ṭhapitāni paṭikkhittāni:
above.english: ‘These positions that are undisclosed, set aside, discarded by the Blessed One…

lines.pali: ‘sassato loko’tipi, ‘asassato loko’tipi …pe…
‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi—
tāni me bhagavā na byākaroti.

below.pali: Yāni me bhagavā na byākaroti taṁ me na ruccati, taṁ me nakkhamati.
below.english: I don’t approve, I don’t accept that the Blessed One has not disclosed them to me.

above.pali: Sace bhagavā jānāti:
above.sujato: If you know

lines.pali: ‘antavā loko’ti, ‘anantavā loko’ti me bhagavā byākarotu;
lines.sujato: that the cosmos is finite,

lines.pali: sace bhagavā jānāti:
‘anantavā loko’ti, ‘anantavā loko’ti me bhagavā byākarotu.
lines.sujato: or infinite;

lines.pali: No ce bhagavā jānāti:
‘antavā loko’ti vā, ‘anantavā loko’ti vā, ajānato kho pana apassato etadeva ujukaṁ hoti yadidaṁ:
‘na jānāmi, na passāmī’ti.
Sace bhagavā jānāti:
‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti, ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti me bhagavā byākarotu;
lines.sujato: that the soul and the body are one and the same,

lines.pali: sace bhagavā jānāti:
‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti, ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti me bhagavā byākarotu.
lines.sujato: or is the soul one thing, the body another;

lines.pali: No ce bhagavā jānāti:
‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti vā, ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti vā, ajānato kho pana apassato etadeva ujukaṁ hoti yadidaṁ:
‘na jānāmi, na passāmī’ti.
Sace bhagavā jānāti:
‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti me bhagavā byākarotu;
lines.sujato: that after death, a realized one still exists,

lines.pali: sace bhagavā jānāti:
‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti me bhagavā byākarotu.
lines.sujato: or no longer exists,

lines.pali: No ce bhagavā jānāti:
‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vā, ajānato kho pana apassato etadeva ujukaṁ hoti yadidaṁ:
‘na jānāmi na passāmī’ti.
Sace bhagavā jānāti:
‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti me bhagavā byākarotu;
lines.sujato: or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists, please tell me.

lines.pali: sace bhagavā jānāti:
‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti me bhagavā byākarotu.

below.pali: No ce bhagavā jānāti:
below.sujato: If you don’t know
below.english: If he doesn’t know or see whether after death a Tathāgata exists… does not exist… both exists & does not exist… neither exists nor does not exist,’

above.pali: ‘Na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso abhavissāti, evampi no.
above.sujato: ‘a realized one no longer exists after death’ …
above.english: And it’s not the case that when there is the view, ‘After death a Tathāgata does not exist,’ there is the living of the holy life.

lines.pali: ‘Hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vā, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vā diṭṭhiyā sati attheva jāti …pe…
yesāhaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme nighātaṁ paññapemi.

below.pali: ‘Hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso abhavissāti, evaṁ no.
below.sujato: ‘a realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death’ …
below.english: And it’s not the case that when there is the view, ‘After death a Tathāgata both exists & does not exist,’ there is the living of the holy life.

above.pali: Vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati vicikicchāparetena;
above.sujato: Their heart is overcome and mired in doubt,
above.english: “He remains with his awareness possessed by uncertainty…

lines.pali: uppannāya ca vicikicchāya nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
lines.sujato: and they don’t truly understand the escape from doubt that has arisen.

lines.pali: Tassa sā vicikicchā thāmagatā appaṭivinītā orambhāgiyaṁ saṁyojanaṁ.
lines.sujato: That doubt is entrenched in them, not eliminated: it is a lower fetter.

below.pali: Sīlabbataparāmāsapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati sīlabbataparāmāsaparetena;
below.sujato: Their heart is overcome and mired in misapprehension of precepts and observances,
below.english: “He remains with his awareness possessed by grasping at habits & practices…

above.pali: Sīlabbataparāmāsapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati sīlabbataparāmāsaparetena;
above.sujato: Their heart is overcome and mired in misapprehension of precepts and observances,
above.english: “He remains with his awareness possessed by grasping at habits & practices…

lines.pali: uppannassa ca sīlabbataparāmāsassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
lines.sujato: and they don’t truly understand the escape from misapprehension of precepts and observances that has arisen.

lines.pali: Tassa so sīlabbataparāmāso thāmagato appaṭivinīto orambhāgiyaṁ saṁyojanaṁ.
lines.sujato: That misapprehension of precepts and observances is entrenched in them, not eliminated: it is a lower fetter.

below.pali: Kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati kāmarāgaparetena;
below.sujato: Their heart is overcome and mired in sensual desire,
below.english: “He remains with his awareness possessed by sensual passion…

above.pali: Kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati kāmarāgaparetena;
above.sujato: Their heart is overcome and mired in sensual desire,
above.english: “He remains with his awareness possessed by sensual passion…

lines.pali: uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
lines.sujato: and they don’t truly understand the escape from sensual desire that has arisen.

lines.pali: Tassa so kāmarāgo thāmagato appaṭivinīto orambhāgiyaṁ saṁyojanaṁ.
lines.sujato: That sensual desire is entrenched in them, not eliminated: it is a lower fetter.

below.pali: Byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati byāpādaparetena;
below.sujato: Their heart is overcome and mired in ill will,
below.english: “He remains with his awareness possessed by ill will, overcome by ill will.

above.pali: Na vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na vicikicchāparetena;
above.sujato: Their heart is not overcome and mired in doubt,
above.english: “He remains with his awareness not possessed by uncertainty…

lines.pali: uppannāya ca vicikicchāya nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
lines.sujato: and they truly understand the escape from doubt that has arisen.

lines.pali: Tassa sā vicikicchā sānusayā pahīyati.
lines.sujato: That doubt, along with any underlying tendency to it, is given up in them.

below.pali: Na sīlabbataparāmāsapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na sīlabbataparāmāsaparetena;
below.sujato: Their heart is not overcome and mired in misapprehension of precepts and observances,
below.english: “He remains with his awareness not possessed by grasping at habits & practices…

below.sujato: Their heart is not overcome and mired in ill will,

above.pali: catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
above.sujato: fourth absorption.
above.english: and fourth jhāna.]

lines.pali: So yadeva tattha hoti rūpagataṁ vedanāgataṁ saññāgataṁ saṅkhāragataṁ viññāṇagataṁ …
lines.sujato: They contemplate the phenomena there—included in form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness—as impermanent …

lines.pali: pe…
lines.sujato: They turn their mind away from those things …

lines.pali: anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.
lines.sujato: If they don’t attain the ending of defilements, they’re reborn spontaneously … and are not liable to return from that world.

lines.pali: Ayampi kho, ānanda, maggo ayaṁ paṭipadā pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ pahānāya.
lines.sujato: This too is the path and the practice for giving up the five lower fetters.

below.pali: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
below.sujato: Furthermore, a mendicant, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.
below.english: “And further, Ānanda, the monk—with the complete transcending of perceptions of (physical) form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and not attending to perceptions of multiplicity, (perceiving,) ‘Infinite space’—enters & remains in the dimension of the infinitude of space.

above.pali: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
above.sujato: Furthermore, a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite consciousness.
above.english: [Similarly with the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness and the dimension of nothingness.]

lines.pali: So yadeva tattha hoti vedanāgataṁ saññāgataṁ saṅkhāragataṁ viññāṇagataṁ …
lines.sujato: They contemplate the phenomena there—included in feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness—as impermanent …

lines.pali: pe…
lines.sujato: They turn their mind away from those things …

lines.pali: anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.
lines.sujato: If they don’t attain the ending of defilements, they’re reborn spontaneously … and are not liable to return from that world.

lines.pali: Ayampi kho, ānanda, maggo ayaṁ paṭipadā pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ pahānāya.
lines.sujato: This too is the path and the practice for giving up the five lower fetters.

below.pali: “Eso ce, bhante, maggo esā paṭipadā pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ pahānāya, atha kiñcarahi idhekacce bhikkhū cetovimuttino ekacce bhikkhū paññāvimuttino”ti?
below.sujato: “Sir, if this is the path and the practice for giving up the five lower fetters, how then are some mendicants here released in heart while others are released by wisdom?”
below.english: “But, lord, if this is the path, if this is the practice, for the abandoning of the five lower fetters, then why are some monks (said to be) ‘released through awareness,’ and some monks are (said to be) ‘released through discernment’?”

above.pali: evameva kho, bhante, santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ, tesaṁ bhagavantaṁ apassantānaṁ siyā aññathattaṁ, siyā vipariṇāmo.
above.sujato: In the same way, there are mendicants here who are junior, recently gone forth, newly come to this teaching and training. If they don’t get to see the Buddha they may change and fall apart.
above.english: in the same way, there are new monks here, not long gone forth, recently arrived at this Dhamma & Vinaya. If they don’t see the Blessed One, there may be a change in them, there may be an alteration.”

lines.pali: Abhinandatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṁ;
lines.sujato: May the Buddha be happy with the mendicant Saṅgha!

lines.pali: abhivadatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṁ.
lines.sujato: May the Buddha welcome the mendicant Saṅgha!

lines.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhante, bhagavatā pubbe bhikkhusaṅgho anuggahito; evameva bhagavā etarahi anuggaṇhātu bhikkhusaṅghan”ti.
lines.sujato: May the Buddha support the mendicant Saṅgha now as he did in the past!”

below.pali: Atha kho brahmā sahampati bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—brahmaloke antarahito bhagavato purato pāturahosi.
below.sujato: Then the divinity Sahampati knew the Buddha’s train of thought. As easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from the realm of divinity and reappeared in front of the Buddha.
below.english: Then Brahmā Sahampati, having known with his own awareness the line of thinking in the Blessed One’s awareness, disappeared from the Brahmā world and—just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm—appeared in front of the Blessed One.

above.pali: evameva kho, bhante, santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ, tesaṁ bhagavantaṁ apassantānaṁ siyā aññathattaṁ, siyā vipariṇāmo.
above.sujato: In the same way, there are mendicants here who are junior, recently gone forth, newly come to this teaching and training. If they don’t get to see the Buddha they may change and fall apart.
above.english: in the same way, there are new monks here, not long gone forth, recently arrived at this Dhamma & Vinaya. If they don’t see the Blessed One, there may be a change in them, there may be an alteration.”

lines.pali: Abhinandatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṁ;
lines.sujato: May the Buddha be happy with the mendicant Saṅgha!

lines.pali: abhivadatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṁ.
lines.sujato: May the Buddha welcome the mendicant Saṅgha!

lines.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhante, bhagavatā pubbe bhikkhusaṅgho anuggahito; evameva bhagavā etarahi anuggaṇhātu bhikkhusaṅghan”ti.
lines.sujato: May the Buddha support the mendicant Saṅgha now as he did in the past!”

below.pali: Asakkhiṁsu kho cātumeyyakā ca sakyā brahmā ca sahampati bhagavantaṁ pasādetuṁ bījūpamena ca taruṇūpamena ca.
below.sujato: The Sakyans of Cātumā and the divinity Sahampati were able to restore the Buddha’s confidence with the similes of the seedlings and the calf.
below.english: And so the Cātumā Sakyans & Brahmā Sahampati were able to reconcile the Blessed One by means of the simile of the seedlings & the simile of the young calf.

above.pali: Yato kho te bhikkhū nāsakkhiṁsu assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū saññāpetuṁ, atha yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
above.sujato: Since those mendicants were unable to persuade the mendicants who were followers of Assaji and Punabbasuka, they approached the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.
above.english: When they were unable to convince the monks led by Assaji & Punabbasu, those monks went to the Blessed One [and told him what had happened].

lines.pali: “idha mayaṁ, bhante, yena assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū etadavocumha:
‘bhagavā kho, āvuso, aññatreva rattibhojanā bhuñjati bhikkhusaṅgho ca;
aññatra kho panāvuso, rattibhojanā bhuñjamānā appābādhatañca sañjānanti appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca.
Etha, tumhepi, āvuso, aññatreva rattibhojanā bhuñjatha.
Aññatra kho panāvuso, tumhepi rattibhojanā bhuñjamānā appābādhatañca sañjānissatha appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañcā’ti.
Evaṁ vutte, bhante, assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū amhe etadavocuṁ:
‘mayaṁ kho, āvuso, sāyañceva bhuñjāma pāto ca divā ca vikāle.
Te mayaṁ sāyañceva bhuñjamānā pāto ca divā ca vikāle appābādhatañca sañjānāma appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca.
Te mayaṁ kiṁ sandiṭṭhikaṁ hitvā kālikaṁ anudhāvissāma?
Sāyañceva mayaṁ bhuñjissāma pāto ca divā ca vikāle’ti.
Yato kho mayaṁ, bhante, nāsakkhimha assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū saññāpetuṁ, atha mayaṁ etamatthaṁ bhagavato ārocemā”ti.

below.pali: Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ āmantesi:
below.sujato: So the Buddha addressed one of the monks,
below.english: Then the Blessed One told a certain monk,

above.pali: “saccaṁ kira, bhikkhave, sambahulā bhikkhū tumhe upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṁ:
above.sujato: The Buddha said to them, “Is it really true, mendicants, that several mendicants went to you and said:
above.english: As they were sitting there, the Blessed One said to him, “Is it true, monks, that a large number of monks went to you…

lines.pali: ‘bhagavā kho, āvuso, aññatreva rattibhojanā bhuñjati bhikkhusaṅgho ca.
lines.sujato: ‘Reverends, the Buddha never eats at night, and neither does the mendicant Saṅgha.

lines.pali: Aññatra kho panāvuso, rattibhojanā bhuñjamānā appābādhatañca sañjānanti appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca.
lines.sujato: Doing so, they find that they’re healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.

lines.pali: Etha, tumhepi, āvuso, aññatreva rattibhojanā bhuñjatha.
lines.sujato: You too should never eat at night.

lines.pali: Aññatra kho panāvuso, tumhepi rattibhojanā bhuñjamānā appābādhatañca sañjānissatha appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañcā’ti.
lines.sujato: Doing so, you’ll find that you’re healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.’

below.pali: Evaṁ vutte, kira, bhikkhave, tumhe te bhikkhū evaṁ avacuttha:
below.sujato: When they said this, did you really say to them:
below.english: and you said,

lines.pali: ‘mayaṁ kho panāvuso, sāyañceva bhuñjāma pāto ca divā ca vikāle.
lines.sujato: ‘Reverends, we eat at dusk, at daybreak, and at the wrong time of day.

lines.pali: Te mayaṁ sāyañceva bhuñjamānā pāto ca divā ca vikāle appābādhatañca sañjānāma appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca.
lines.sujato: Doing so, we find that we’re healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.

below.pali: Te mayaṁ kiṁ sandiṭṭhikaṁ hitvā kālikaṁ anudhāvissāma?
below.sujato: Why should we give up what is apparent in the present to chase after what takes effect over time?
below.english: ‘…Why should we, abandoning what is immediately visible, chase after something subject to time?

above.pali: Mayā cetaṁ, bhikkhave, aññātaṁ abhavissa adiṭṭhaṁ aviditaṁ asacchikataṁ aphassitaṁ paññāya:
above.sujato: Now, suppose I hadn’t known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:
above.english: [Similarly for painful feelings and neither-pleasant-nor-painful feelings.]

lines.pali: ‘idhekaccassa evarūpaṁ dukkhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evāhaṁ ajānanto ‘evarūpaṁ dukkhaṁ vedanaṁ pajahathā’ti vadeyyaṁ;
lines.sujato: ‘When someone feels this kind of painful feeling, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decline.’

lines.pali: api nu me etaṁ, bhikkhave, patirūpaṁ abhavissā”ti?
lines.sujato: Not knowing this, would it be appropriate for me to say: ‘You should give up this kind of painful feeling’?”

below.pali: Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sabbesaṁyeva bhikkhūnaṁ ‘appamādena karaṇīyan’ti vadāmi;
below.sujato: Mendicants, I don’t say that all these mendicants still have work to do with diligence.
below.english: “Monks, I don’t say of all monks that they have a task to do with heedfulness;

above.pali: “‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, sassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
above.sujato: “Worthy Gotama, when asked these ten questions, you say: ‘That’s not my view.’
above.english: “How is it, Master Gotama, when Master Gotama is asked if he holds the view ‘the cosmos is eternal…’ … ‘after death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist: only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless,’ he says ‘ … no…’ in each case.

lines.pali: evaṁdiṭṭhi bhavaṁ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṁ, vaccha, evaṁdiṭṭhi—
sassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, asassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
evaṁdiṭṭhi bhavaṁ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṁ, vaccha, evaṁdiṭṭhi—
asassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, antavā loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
evaṁdiṭṭhi bhavaṁ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṁ, vaccha, evaṁdiṭṭhi—
antavā loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, anantavā loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
evaṁdiṭṭhi bhavaṁ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṁ, vaccha, evaṁdiṭṭhi—
anantavā loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīraṁ, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
evaṁdiṭṭhi bhavaṁ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṁ, vaccha, evaṁdiṭṭhi—
taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīraṁ, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīraṁ, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
evaṁdiṭṭhi bhavaṁ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṁ, vaccha, evaṁdiṭṭhi—
aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīraṁ, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
evaṁdiṭṭhi bhavaṁ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṁ, vaccha, evaṁdiṭṭhi—
hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
evaṁdiṭṭhi bhavaṁ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṁ, vaccha, evaṁdiṭṭhi—
na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
evaṁdiṭṭhi bhavaṁ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṁ, vaccha, evaṁdiṭṭhi—
hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
evaṁdiṭṭhi bhavaṁ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṁ, vaccha, evaṁdiṭṭhi—
neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.

below.pali: Kiṁ pana bho gotamo ādīnavaṁ sampassamāno evaṁ imāni sabbaso diṭṭhigatāni anupagato”ti?
below.sujato: Seeing what drawback do you avoid all these convictions?”
below.english: Seeing what drawback, then, is Master Gotama thus entirely dissociated from each of these ten positions?”

above.pali: “‘Evaṁ vimuttacitto pana, bho gotama, bhikkhu kuhiṁ upapajjatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upetī’ti vadesi.
above.sujato: “Worthy Gotama, when asked all these questions, you say: ‘It doesn’t apply.’
above.english: “How is it, Master Gotama, when Master Gotama is asked if the monk reappears… does not reappear… both does & does not reappear… neither does nor does not reappear, he says, ‘… doesn’t apply’ in each case.

lines.pali: ‘Tena hi, bho gotama, na upapajjatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upetī’ti vadesi.
‘Tena hi, bho gotama, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upetī’ti vadesi.
‘Tena hi, bho gotama, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upetī’ti vadesi.

below.sujato: Some time later—having truly understood the origin, ending, gratification, drawback, and escape of sensual pleasures, and having given up craving and dispelled passion for sensual pleasures—I live rid of thirst, my mind settled internally.

lines.pali: kāyaviññeyyehi phoṭṭhabbehi iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṁhitehi rajanīyehi.
lines.sujato: touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

below.pali: So aparena samayena kāmānaṁyeva samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ viditvā kāmataṇhaṁ pahāya kāmapariḷāhaṁ paṭivinodetvā vigatapipāso ajjhattaṁ vūpasantacitto viharāmi.
below.sujato: Some time later—having truly understood the origin, ending, gratification, drawback, and escape of sensual pleasures, and having given up craving and dispelled passion for sensual pleasures—I live rid of thirst, my mind settled internally.
below.english: “But having known at a later time—as they have come to be—the origination, the passing away, the allure, the drawbacks, & the escape from those very same sensualities, I now dwell having abandoned craving for sensuality, having removed fever for sensuality, free from thirst, my mind inwardly at peace.

above.pali: “Seyyathāpi, māgaṇḍiya, jaccandho puriso;
above.sujato: “Māgaṇḍiya, suppose a person was blind from birth.
above.english: “Māgaṇḍiya, it’s just as if there were a man blind from birth who couldn’t see black objects… white… blue… yellow… red… or pink objects; who couldn’t see even or uneven places, the stars, the sun, or the moon.

lines.pali: so na passeyya kaṇhasukkāni rūpāni, na passeyya nīlakāni rūpāni, na passeyya pītakāni rūpāni, na passeyya lohitakāni rūpāni, na passeyya mañjiṭṭhakāni rūpāni, na passeyya samavisamaṁ, na passeyya tārakarūpāni, na passeyya candimasūriye.
lines.sujato: They couldn’t see sights that are dark or bright, or blue, yellow, red, or magenta. They couldn’t see even and uneven ground, or the stars, or the moon and sun.

lines.pali: So suṇeyya cakkhumato bhāsamānassa:
lines.sujato: They might hear a sighted person saying:

lines.pali: ‘chekaṁ vata, bho, odātaṁ vatthaṁ abhirūpaṁ nimmalaṁ sucī’ti.
lines.sujato: ‘White cloth is really nice, it’s attractive, stainless, and clean.’

below.pali: Tamenaṁ aññataro puriso telamalikatena sāhuḷicīrena vañceyya:
below.sujato: But someone would cheat them with a dirty, soiled garment, saying:
below.english: Now, suppose that a certain man were to take a grimy, oil-stained rag and fool him, saying,

above.pali: nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa;
above.sujato: This Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan leads an order and a community, and tutors a community. He’s a well-known and famous religious founder, deemed holy by many people.
above.english: & Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta.]

lines.pali: so ca kho sāvakānaṁ na sakkato na garukato na mānito na pūjito, na ca pana nigaṇṭhaṁ nāṭaputtaṁ sāvakā sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya viharanti.
lines.sujato: But he’s not honored, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples. And his disciples, not honoring and respecting him, don’t remain loyal to him.

lines.pali: Bhūtapubbaṁ nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto anekasatāya parisāya dhammaṁ deseti.
lines.sujato: Once it so happened that he was teaching an assembly of many hundreds.

lines.pali: Tatraññataro nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa sāvako saddamakāsi:
lines.sujato: Then one of his disciples made a noise,

lines.pali: “mā bhonto nigaṇṭhaṁ nāṭaputtaṁ etamatthaṁ pucchittha;
lines.sujato: “My good fellows, don’t ask the Jain Ñātika about that.

lines.pali: neso etaṁ jānāti;
lines.sujato: He doesn’t know that.

lines.pali: mayametaṁ jānāma, amhe etamatthaṁ pucchatha;
lines.sujato: I know it. Ask me about it,

lines.pali: mayametaṁ bhavantānaṁ byākarissāmā”ti.
lines.sujato: and I’ll answer you.”

lines.pali: Bhūtapubbaṁ nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto bāhā paggayha kandanto na labhati:
lines.sujato: Once it so happened that the Jain Ñātika didn’t get his way, though he called out with raised arms,

lines.pali: “appasaddā bhonto hontu, mā bhonto saddamakattha.
lines.sujato: “Be quiet, good fellows, don’t make a sound.

lines.pali: Nete bhavante pucchanti, amhe ete pucchanti;
lines.sujato: They’re not asking you, they’re asking me!

lines.pali: mayametesaṁ byākarissāmā”ti.
lines.sujato: I’ll answer you!”

lines.pali: Bahū kho pana nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa sāvakā vādaṁ āropetvā apakkantā:
lines.sujato: Indeed, many of his disciples have left him after refuting his doctrine:

lines.pali: “na tvaṁ imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ ājānāsi, ahaṁ imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ ājānāmi. Kiṁ tvaṁ imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ ājānissasi? Micchāpaṭipanno tvamasi. Ahamasmi sammāpaṭipanno. Sahitaṁ me asahitaṁ te, purevacanīyaṁ pacchā avaca, pacchāvacanīyaṁ pure avaca, adhiciṇṇaṁ te viparāvattaṁ, āropito te vādo, niggahitosi, cara vādappamokkhāya, nibbeṭhehi vā sace pahosī”ti.
lines.sujato: “You don’t understand this teaching and training. I understand this teaching and training. What, you understand this teaching and training? You’re practicing wrong. I’m practicing right. I stay on topic, you don’t. You said last what you should have said first. You said first what you should have said last. What you’ve thought so much about has been disproved. Your doctrine is refuted. Go on, save your doctrine! You’re trapped; get yourself out of this—if you can!”

lines.pali: Iti nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto sāvakānaṁ na sakkato na garukato na mānito na pūjito, na ca pana nigaṇṭhaṁ nāṭaputtaṁ sāvakā sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya viharanti.
lines.sujato: That’s how the Jain Ñātika is not honored, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples. On the contrary, his disciples, not honoring and respecting him, don’t remain loyal to him.

lines.pali: Akkuṭṭho ca pana nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto dhammakkosenā’ti.
lines.sujato: Rather, he’s reviled, and rightly so.’

below.pali: Ekacce evamāhaṁsu:
below.sujato: Others said:
below.english: “Then some said this,

above.pali: sappāṭihāriyaṁ samaṇo gotamo dhammaṁ deseti no appāṭihāriyan’ti.
above.sujato: He teaches with a demonstrable basis, not without it.’
above.english: It’s with marvels that he teaches the Dhamma, not without marvels.’

lines.pali: Yampudāyi, mamaṁ sāvakā abhikkante ñāṇadassane sambhāventi:
lines.sujato: Since this is so,

lines.pali: ‘jānaṁyevāha samaṇo gotamo—jānāmīti,
passaṁyevāha samaṇo gotamo—passāmīti;
abhiññāya samaṇo gotamo dhammaṁ deseti no anabhiññāya;
sanidānaṁ samaṇo gotamo dhammaṁ deseti no anidānaṁ;

below.pali: sappāṭihāriyaṁ samaṇo gotamo dhammaṁ deseti no appāṭihāriyan’ti, ayaṁ kho, udāyi, dutiyo dhammo yena mamaṁ sāvakā sakkaronti garuṁ karonti mānenti pūjenti, sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya viharanti.
below.sujato: this is the second quality because of which my disciples are loyal to me.
below.english: This is the second quality…

above.pali: dukkhanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ ariyasaccaṁ pucchanti, tesāhaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ ariyasaccaṁ puṭṭho byākaromi, tesāhaṁ cittaṁ ārādhemi pañhassa veyyākaraṇena.
above.sujato: and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering apply to the suffering  in which they are swamped and mired. And I provide them with satisfying answers to their questions.
above.english: the noble truth of the path of practice leading to the cessation of suffering. I, being asked, explain the noble truth of the path of practice leading to the cessation of suffering and I satisfy their minds with my answer.

lines.pali: Yampudāyi, mama sāvakā yena dukkhena dukkhotiṇṇā dukkhaparetā te maṁ upasaṅkamitvā dukkhaṁ ariyasaccaṁ pucchanti, tesāhaṁ dukkhaṁ ariyasaccaṁ puṭṭho byākaromi, tesāhaṁ cittaṁ ārādhemi pañhassa veyyākaraṇena.
lines.sujato: Since this is so,

dukkhanirodhaṁ …

above.pali: Na tvaṁ, tāta raṭṭhapāla, kassaci, dukkhassa jānāsi.
above.sujato: You know nothing of suffering.
above.english: You know nothing of suffering.

lines.sujato: When you die we will lose you against our wishes.

lines.pali: Kiṁ pana mayaṁ taṁ jīvantaṁ anujānissāma agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjāya.
lines.sujato: So how can we allow you to go forth from lay life to homelessness while you’re still living?

below.pali: Uṭṭhehi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, bhuñja ca piva ca paricārehi ca;
below.sujato: Get up, Raṭṭhapāla! Eat, drink, and amuse yourself.
below.english: Get up, dear. Eat, drink, & enjoy yourself.

above.pali: “tvaṁ khosi, samma raṭṭhapāla, mātāpitūnaṁ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparibhato.
above.sujato: “Our dear Raṭṭhapāla, you are your parents’ only child. You’re dear to them and they love you. You’re pampered and raised in comfort.
above.english: “Friend Raṭṭhapāla, you are your parents’ only son…

lines.sujato: So how can they allow you to go forth while you’re still alive?

lines.sujato: While enjoying sensual pleasures, delight in making merit.

lines.sujato: Your parents will not allow you to go forth.

below.pali: Kiṁ pana te taṁ jīvantaṁ anujānissanti agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjāyā”ti?
below.sujato: So how can they allow you to go forth while you’re still alive?”
below.english: How could your parents—while you’re alive—give their permission for you to go forth from the household life into homelessness?”

above.pali: “Evameva kho, rājakumāra, ye hi keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā kāyena ceva cittena ca kāmehi avūpakaṭṭhā viharanti, yo ca nesaṁ kāmesu kāmacchando kāmasneho kāmamucchā kāmapipāsā kāmapariḷāho so ca ajjhattaṁ na suppahīno hoti, na suppaṭippassaddho.
above.sujato: “In the same way, there are ascetics and brahmins who don’t live withdrawn in body and mind from sensual pleasures. They haven’t internally given up or stilled desire, affection, infatuation, thirst, and passion for sensual pleasures. Regardless of whether or not they suffer painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings due to exertion, they are incapable of knowledge and vision, of supreme awakening.
above.english: “So it is, prince, with any contemplative or brahman who does not live withdrawn from sensuality in body & mind, and whose desire, infatuation, urge, thirst, & fever for sensuality is not relinquished & stilled within him: Whether or not he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings (due to his striving for awakening), he is incapable of knowledge, vision, & unexcelled self-awakening.

lines.pali: Opakkamikā cepi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedayanti, abhabbāva te ñāṇāya dassanāya anuttarāya sambodhāya.
No cepi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedayanti, abhabbāva te ñāṇāya dassanāya anuttarāya sambodhāya.

below.pali: Ayaṁ kho maṁ, rājakumāra, paṭhamā upamā paṭibhāsi anacchariyā pubbe assutapubbā.
below.sujato: This was the first example that occurred to me.
below.english: This was the first simile—spontaneous, never before heard—that appeared to me.

above.pali: “Evameva kho, rājakumāra, ye hi keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā kāyena ceva cittena ca kāmehi vūpakaṭṭhā viharanti, yo ca nesaṁ kāmesu kāmacchando kāmasneho kāmamucchā kāmapipāsā kāmapariḷāho so ca ajjhattaṁ na suppahīno hoti, na suppaṭippassaddho.
above.sujato: “In the same way, there are ascetics and brahmins who live withdrawn in body and mind from sensual pleasures. But they haven’t internally given up or stilled desire, affection, infatuation, thirst, and passion for sensual pleasures. Regardless of whether or not they suffer painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings due to exertion, they are incapable of knowledge and vision, of supreme awakening.
above.english: “So it is, prince, with any contemplative or brahman who lives withdrawn from sensuality in body only, but whose desire, infatuation, urge, thirst, & fever for sensuality is not relinquished & stilled within him: Whether or not he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings (due to his striving), he is incapable of knowledge, vision, & unexcelled self-awakening.

above.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma kammāragaggariyā dhamamānāya adhimatto saddo hoti;
above.sujato: like the puffing of a blacksmith’s bellows.
above.english: just like the loud roar of winds coming out of a smith’s bellows.…

lines.pali: evameva kho me, rājakumāra, mukhato ca nāsato ca assāsapassāsesu uparuddhesu kaṇṇasotehi vātānaṁ nikkhamantānaṁ adhimatto saddo hoti.
Āraddhaṁ kho pana me, rājakumāra, vīriyaṁ hoti asallīnaṁ, upaṭṭhitā sati asammuṭṭhā, sāraddho ca pana me kāyo hoti appaṭippassaddho, teneva dukkhappadhānena padhānābhitunnassa sato.
lines.sujato: My energy was roused up and unflagging, and my mindfulness was established and lucid, but my body was disturbed, not tranquil, because I’d pushed too hard with that painful striving.

below.pali: So kho ahaṁ, rājakumāra, mukhato ca nāsato ca kaṇṇato ca assāsapassāse uparundhiṁ.
below.sujato: So I cut off my breathing through my mouth and nose and ears.
below.english: So I stopped the in-breaths & out-breaths in my nose & mouth & ears.

above.pali: Seyyathāpi, rājakumāra, balavā puriso tiṇhena sikharena muddhani abhimattheyya;
above.sujato: like a strong man was drilling into my head with a sharp point.
above.english: just as if a strong man were slicing my head open with a sharp sword.…

above.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, asappuriso bahussuto hoti.

lines.pali: So iti paṭisañcikkhati:
‘ahaṁ khomhi bahussuto, ime panaññe bhikkhū na bahussutā’ti.
So tena bāhusaccena attānukkaṁseti, paraṁ vambheti.
Ayampi, bhikkhave, asappurisadhammo.
Sappuriso ca kho, bhikkhave, iti paṭisañcikkhati:
‘na kho bāhusaccena lobhadhammā vā parikkhayaṁ gacchanti, dosadhammā vā parikkhayaṁ gacchanti, mohadhammā vā parikkhayaṁ gacchanti.
No cepi bahussuto hoti;
so ca hoti dhammānudhammappaṭipanno sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī, so tattha pujjo, so tattha pāsaṁso’ti.
So paṭipadaṁyeva antaraṁ karitvā tena bāhusaccena nevattānukkaṁseti, na paraṁ vambheti.
Ayampi, bhikkhave, sappurisadhammo.
